abundance-dependency.question: Does {target.symbol} PROTEIN abundance predict its own dependency across cell lines — is protein abundance a biomarker of dependency (and does it beat the RNA arm)?
caveats: PROTEIN arm of the expression-as-biomarker-of-dependency question; the RNA arm is the sibling card expression-dependency-correlation. Report side-by-side, NEVER averaged — their disagreement picks the preferred dependency-biomarker assay (RNA vs protein) in synthesis.

A WEAK abundance→dependency link is NOT a target negative: for oncogene-addiction targets (e.g. KRAS) dependency is driven by MUTATION status, not protein abundance, so the abundance biomarker is correctly weak and synthesis should prefer the genomic stratifier (mutation-stratified-dependency). Interpret alongside that card.
Gygi MS quantifies ~12.5k proteins; a target absent from the panel yields data_unavailable (protein_panel_size / n_protein_detected_models reflect panel coverage, not biology).
Correlation reflects cell-line behavior; abundance-stratification in vivo may differ (microenvironment, heterogeneity). A strong negative r is necessary but not sufficient for a clinical biomarker.
Sign convention: NEGATIVE Pearson r = higher protein → lower Chronos = more dependent (matches the RNA card's convention).

warning_predicates.message: Letter grades were SUPPRESSED for {target.symbol}. Upstream surface-topology-and-ptm card flagged a clinically-dominant alt isoform — see that card's warnings for isoform-specific context. Do not cite letter grades in decks; use fit_class biology-agnostic categorical instead.
Letter grade sits near a rubric threshold (bootstrap perturbation ±20% flips the grade). Governance readers should treat the grade as tier-boundary rather than a settled call.

Both ADC and TCE grades are A or B, or biology signals conflict. Biology context (indication, ligand-independence, resistance emergence) is needed to disambiguate — modality lens output alone is insufficient.

caveats:
fit_class is BIOLOGY-AGNOSTIC and emitted unconditionally. Letter grades
(adc_grade, tce_grade, adc_score, tce_score) are LENS-CONDITIONAL — emitted
only when the `--modality` lens is invoked at target-profile runtime.
Invocations without the modality lens produce biology-first output only.
This is enforced by the card.schema.json arch A2 extension.
Rubric weights are exposed in modality_rubric.yaml (versioned, editable
per-program). Governance readers can reproduce any letter grade from
(rubric_version, biology inputs). Rubric weight tuning is a governance
decision, not a per-target decision.
Isoform-selective suppression (arch A3): if surface-topology-and-ptm
flags the target as having a clinically-dominant alt isoform in the
isoform_selective_targets vocabulary, letter grades are suppressed
regardless of modality-lens invocation. fit_class becomes
'isoform_dependent_undefined' to force isoform-resolved reasoning.
Verification Test 5 (rigor R3): rubric grades are benchmarked against
a curated clinical-precedent anchor set (~30 known-ADC + ~20 known-TCE
clinical-precedented targets). If concordance drops < 80% AUROC on
that anchor set, letter grades ship as `_validation_status:
exploratory_not_benchmark_validated` in provenance.
Grade stability is bootstrap-computed by perturbing each rubric weight
by ±20%. 'sensitive' means the grade tier shifts under perturbation —
treat as tier-boundary. 'stable' means grade holds across the full
perturbation range.

alteration-clinical-association.question: Does {target.symbol} somatic-mutation status stratify overall survival in {indication.label} — is a {target.symbol} mutation a candidate prognostic marker (mutated worse or better OS)?
caveats: HYPOTHESIS-GENERATING, NOT a clinical claim: a univariate mutation-status log-rank UNADJUSTED for stage/age/grade. Survival is stage-dominated; a single-gene mutation split rarely reaches significance and, when it does, may be confounded. Necessary-but-not-sufficient — needs a multivariable Cox model + orthogonal validation.
MUTATION status only (SNV/indel from MC3). CN-loss/amp and fusion arms are a follow-on — a target whose prognostic alteration is copy-number or a fusion will read no_survival_association here.
WT = an MC3-PROFILED indication patient with no {target} mutation (cohort denominator = the product's indication column). A patient not profiled by MC3 is absent from the cohort, not mis-called WT.
A rare mutation (few mutated patients) is reported as insufficient_survival_data, never a spurious claim (min_per_arm floor).
OS only in this slice (CDR also carries PFI/DSS/DFI). median_ostime_*_days are raw medians for context, NOT Kaplan-Meier estimates.
alteration_mutated_better_survival is NOT a target killer — it flags that the prognostic/selection rationale differs; interpret alongside the dependency + genomic-driver evidence.

alteration-role.question: Is {target.symbol} a functional cancer driver in {indication.label} — activating (GoF) driver, loss-of-function (LoF) driver, predictive biomarker, or passenger — and by what driver-annotation evidence?
caveats: FUNCTIONAL-ROLE call, not a frequency — a gene can be frequently mutated (mutation-hotspot-frequency) yet a passenger here, or an infrequent-but-bona-fide driver. Interpret alongside the frequency/CN cards.

OncoKB public endpoint is GENE-level (geneType); per-VARIANT oncogenicity is auth-gated and NOT used. So the role is a gene-level driver call, not a variant-specific one — a passenger mutation in a driver gene still reads as the gene's role.

IntOGen mode-of-action is statistical (dN/dS-family + clustering across cohorts); indication scope uses CANCER_TYPE mapping — an indication with no matching IntOGen cohort falls back to pan_cancer scope (still a driver call, just not indication-specific).

predictive_biomarker = the role is ambiguous/bidirectional (OncoKB ONCOGENE_AND_TSG, or OncoKB/IntOGen direction conflict) — actionable as a marker but the GoF/LoF direction is unresolved, NOT a clean driver call. On a source CONFLICT functional_direction is `ambiguous` too, so the record cannot report 'direction unresolved' and a definite direction simultaneously (80 genes did before 2026-09-12: 41 TSGs as activating, 39 oncogenes as loss_of_function).

curated_cancer_gene = OncoKB curates a DIRECTIONAL role (ONCOGENE or TSG) but the gene has ZERO rows in IntOGen — no significant driver call in ANY cohort. Curated cancer-gene status is real evidence and is NOT passenger; it just does not support a 'driver in this indication' claim. 440 of 1242 OncoKB genes are here (283 ONCOGENE + 157 TSG). For surface antigens (CD19, FOLR1, TACSTD2) this is the EXPECTED call — their rationale is lineage expression, not genomic driver status.

alteration_role == direct_driver_gof requires patient-scale (IntOGen) driver evidence, so it is the token that legitimately feeds allele-selective eligibility (wt_loss_safety_conditioning.yaml). Do NOT widen that eligibility to curated_cancer_gene: an OncoKB-list-only gene has no measured activating lesion to select against, which is the same failure mode the amplification disqualifier guards.

A direction from IntOGen requires a 2:1 dominance across the gene's per-cohort ROLE rows. 274 of 633 IntOGen driver genes (43%) carry BOTH Act and LoF rows, so a bare majority manufactures a direction from a near-tie (ROS1 {LoF:3, Act:2} read loss_of_function). See the sweep in the next caveat.

Directional precision against curated direction is FLAT across thresholds (0.744 at 1:1, 0.766 at 3:1) and unanimity is WORST (0.690) — because residual conflicts concentrate in single-cohort genes — so the 2:1 dominance ratio is chosen for consistency with recurrent_event_dominant_ratio, not tuned for precision. The conflict rule above, not the threshold, is what handles contradiction.
passenger = known to a source but with no driver role (OncoKB NEITHER/INSUFFICIENT, no significant IntOGen call); data_unavailable = absent from both sources entirely.

amp-expr-stratified-dependency.question: Is dependency on {target.symbol} stratified by whether the cell line is BOTH copy-number-amplified AND high-expression for {target.symbol} across the DepMap panel? (Amplification-driven overexpression-addiction hypothesis.)

figures.description: Per-cell-line Chronos strip plot split into Amplified+Overexpressed (CN>2.0 AND top-tertile TPM) / Comparator groups. Reference lines at Chronos = -1.0 + 0. Annotated with the q-value + delta.

warning_predicates.message: Fewer than 10 amplified+overexpressed cell lines; conjoint-stratification estimate has wide CI. Interpret amp_expr_stratification_class cautiously.

Amp+overexpr-vs-rest difference is statistically significant but sub-threshold in effect size (delta > -0.2) — at panel n, small deltas reach significance; not classified as stratified (significance != actionable effect). Live example: EGFR (q sig, delta -0.15).

caveats: The positive arm is the CONJUNCTION: amplified (relative CN > 2.0, focal HIGH-LEVEL amp convention; diploid ~ 1.0, NOT log2) AND high-expression (log2TPM in the top within-panel tertile among evaluated lines). Amplified-but-low-expression and high-expression-but-not-amplified lines are EXCLUDED from the positive arm (the AND-gate) — this is what isolates amplification-DRIVEN overexpression from either signal alone.

The high-expression cut is TARGET-RELATIVE (top tertile among the lines with all three measurements), not an absolute TPM. It adapts per target; the exact cut is emitted as high_expression_log2tpm_threshold for provenance.

Two directional passes: a FORWARD one-sided MW (amp+overexpr more dependent) drives the amplified_overexpressed_*_dependent classes; a SECOND-PASS reverse MW (comparator more dependent) makes `amp_expr_negative_more_dependent` reachable, gated on its own BH q + a strong positive delta (>= +0.5). The conjunction is never credited with a dependency it lacks (forward classes cannot fire on a reverse pattern); the reverse class is verdict-inert.

This is the amp→expression→dependency THREE-WAY: it is the conjoint refinement copy-number-stratified-dependency's caveat named. When BOTH copy-number-stratified-dependency (amplified-vs-neutral) and this conjoint class stratify, the resolver's CN rung takes precedence (driving_rule names the CN path); the conjoint rung is placed LAST (most specific) so any single-alteration driver names the verdict first.

Cell-line conjoint-stratified dependency is necessary but NOT sufficient for a clinical biomarker — needs orthogonal validation (isogenic amplification models, patient copy-number + expression). It is not a mediation test: it establishes that the amplified+overexpressed subset is more dependent, not formally that expression MEDIATES the amp→dependency effect.

antigen-internalization.question: Is {target.symbol}'s surface antigen INTERNALIZED upon antibody binding (receptor-mediated endocytosis efficient enough for ADC payload delivery), and what is its surface turnover — the measured axis distinguishing ADC-viable from TCE-only?
caveats:
Internalization discriminates MODALITY, it does not gate the target. An ADC
requires receptor-mediated endocytosis to deliver payload; a T-cell engager /
naked antibody acts at the surface and does NOT. non_internalizing_surface_stable
is therefore a route-to-TCE signal, never a target killer.
ASYMMETRY (load-bearing): absence of an internalization measurement is a WEAK
negative (unmeasured) — NEVER proof the antigen is non-internalizing. Only a
measured assay or a clinical-ADC precedent establishes internalization; a target
not covered stays 'unmeasured' (the honest coverage gap, mirroring pmhc / shed).
The clinical_precedent tier is grounded in approved / late-clinical ADCs against
the antigen (internalizing_antigen_targets.yaml) — an ADC that delivers payload
is internalizing by definition. A citable regulatory/trial crosswalk, NOT a
research-grade 'may internalize' prediction; it supplies positives only.
This card SUPERSEDES the hardcoded-null endocytosis field in adc-tce-modality-fit:
once wired it feeds that composed card as a derived_from input, replacing
endocytosis_confidence='unmeasured' with a measured / clinical-precedent read.

antigen-prevalence-protein.question: What fraction of {indication.label} tumors express {target.symbol} at the PROTEIN level above an ADC/TCE-relevant threshold (not the RNA upper bound)?
caveats:
Protein-level prevalence is the GATING clinical read for a surface-antigen
program; RNA-derived prevalence (antigen-prevalence card) is an UPPER BOUND.
Where the two disagree, protein is the sharper patient-selection estimate —
the framework surfaces both under surface_discordance, never averaged.
CPTAC TMT relative-abundance thresholding is NOT a clinical IHC assay. It
estimates the protein-positive fraction from mass-spec cohort intensities;
a deployable IHC/companion-diagnostic cutoff is a separate downstream question.
MS coverage ASYMMETRY: a peptide below MS detection is not proof the protein
is absent (abundance x digestibility x ionization). A low fraction from sparse
MS coverage is a weak negative; n_samples_protein and protein_evidence_tier
qualify the read.
Prevalence thresholds are iter-1 conservative defaults; modality-specific
calibration (different cutoffs for ADC high-payload vs TCE) is iter-2 work.

antigen-prevalence.question: What fraction of {indication.label} tumors express {target.symbol} at clinically relevant levels?
caveats: Prevalence thresholds are iter-1b conservative defaults; modality-specific calibration is iter-2 work (different thresholds for ADC vs BiTE/TCE).
RNA-derived prevalence is an upper-bound estimate; protein-level prevalence (via IHC) is typically narrower and is the gating clinical question.
Patient-selection biomarker development requires a deployable assay; iter-1b cannot assess assay feasibility.

caf-compartment-expression-luo.question: Across pan-cancer tumour cancer-associated-fibroblast states (Luo atlas), in how many CAF subtypes is {target.symbol} detected, and which CAF state (myCAF / iCAF / apCAF / ...) carries it?

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} is broadly detected on tumour cancer-associated fibroblasts — a stromal/CAF-directed context signal (display-only). Separate this from tumour-cell-intrinsic expression before a tumour-cell-targeted modality call.

caveats: VERDICT-INERT display/context card for the immune-context stromal/CAF lens. Fires no interpretation rule and moves no gate verdict; it adds pan-cancer CAF-state context alongside the CD8 effector-context call.

Pan-cancer, target-grain: the Luo atlas cancer_type axis (lung/PDAC/bladder/thyroid/colorectal/gastric/breast/ovarian/prostate/ICC, tumour-group fibroblasts only) is a pan-cancer stromal readout, NOT a framework-indication scope. The indication is echoed but does not filter the summary.

detection_fraction is single-cell-native (fraction of a CAF state's cells with count>0) and is NOT comparable to bulk TPM; scRNA dropout under-detects. CAF subtypes come from the atlas fibroblast subcluster crosswalk (c1..c8 -> CAFmyo/CAFinfla/CAFadi/CAFEndMT/CAFPN/CAFap + NIF).

RNA detection does not imply protein presence; pair with the surface/protein cards. NIF (normal infiltrating fibroblast) is retained as a subtype for the stroma-vs-CAF contrast; minor CAF states (CAFPN/CAFap/CAFEndMT) are present in only a subset of cancers.

cellline-methylation-expression-coherenc.question: Across DepMap cell lines, does {target.symbol}'s own promoter methylation predict its own LOW expression (epigenetic silencing) — driven by a hypermethylated subset, or broadly?

warning_predicates.message: Fewer than 50 cell lines with both methylation + expression; the silencing estimate has a wide CI.
No hypermethylated subset AND no broad methylation variation; silencing is untestable in this panel → methylation_invariant_panel (honest untestable, NOT uncoupled).

caveats: Silencing is a SUBSET phenomenon: the PRIMARY test is a hypermethylated-subset-vs-rest Mann-Whitney (min_hypermethylated lines), because a minority methylated tail dilutes the pan-panel correlation. Live: MLH1 pan-panel spearman r=-0.02 (null) but subset Δ=-4.62 (p=1.5e-15) — the subset path is what makes subtype-silenced tumor-suppressors detectable. silencing_driver records which path fired.

methylation_invariant_panel (no hypermethylated subset AND no broad variation) is NOT methylation_uncoupled: the silencing question is untestable in this panel (the gene is uniformly (un)methylated), not that methylation fails to silence it. GAPDH/KRAS live here (never hypermethylated).

silencing_lineage_confounded is a MEASURED class, not a data gap: the subset contrast is large and significant but COLLAPSES within lineage (lineage_collapse_ratio < 0.35), so what was measured is lineage separation — a non-expressing lineage that is also a methylated lineage — not promoter silencing. NEUTRAL to the resolver: neither a silencing claim nor a refutation, because no within-lineage-powered silencing test was run on the gene.

lineage_collapse_ratio calibration: CDH1 (-4.44 pan → -0.45 within lineage, ratio 0.10) and MET (-4.99 → -0.85, 0.17) are confounded; the validated silenced suppressors are not (MLH1 0.85, MGMT 0.84, CDKN2A 1.80). The 0.35 floor sits in that gap, and max_lineage_collapse_ratio only applies once the pan-panel delta clears min_pan_delta_for_collapse_check.

The broad-correlation path is a strict FALLBACK, not an alternative: available ONLY when no powered hypermethylated subset exists. A powered subset contrast that fails the moderate delta floor IS the answer, and a diluted panel-wide correlation must not overturn it (AR: 164 hypermethylated lines, subset delta -0.08, yet r=-0.38 p<1e-25 drove silencing_coupled_moderate). The broad path also requires a real effect size — methylation-quartile delta <= -0.5 — not significance alone.

This establishes the feature→LOW-expression (epigenetic-LoF) leg. A silenced gene is NOT a self-dependency — the cis_coherence resolver routes this to coherent_epigenetic_silencing (a synthetic-lethal / silenced-target hypothesis flag), NOT the amplification-addiction dependency cross-tab.

Cell-line RRBS methylation ≈ patient methylation but differs (culture, purity). The patient promoter-methylation arm (tcga-sesame-promoter-methylation-v1 joined via the sample-id crosswalk) is the orthogonal validation leg.
CCLE→DepMap join is via StrippedCellLineName (CCLE NAME_TISSUE → NAME); a small number of lines may not map and are dropped (reported via n_cell_lines_evaluated).

caveats: cis-dosage coupling is CORRELATIONAL, not a formal mediation test: a strong CN↔expression correlation is consistent with amplification driving expression, but a co-amplified neighbor or a shared trans-regulator can produce the same signal. It establishes the feature→expression LEG of the coherence chain, not sole causality.

cn_dosage_uncoupled (CN varies but does not predict expression) is the informative NEGATIVE: it says expression is copy-number-INDEPENDENT (trans/lineage-regulated). Combined with a dependency signal in the cis-coherence resolver, it routes to dependency_without_cis_dosage (a trans-driven, not amplification-driven, dependency).

cn_invariant_panel is NOT cn_dosage_uncoupled: no CN variation means untestable, not that the feature fails to drive expression. A distinct honest bin so the resolver abstains. The untestable gate keys on the p90-p10 spread, NOT the IQR — focal-amp oncogenes (ERBB2/MYC) are bulk-diploid with an amplified tail (IQR ~0 but real tail signal); IQR-gating wrongly called them invariant (fix 2026-08-20).
relative CN is focal-amp convention (diploid ~ 1.0, NOT log2), matching depmap_cn_distribution / amp-expr-stratified-dependency; log2TPM is log2(TPM+1) bulk mRNA (not protein).

cis_dosage_direction names WHICH CN arm carries the coupling — an amplification-driven driver (amplification_coupled) vs a deletion-driven suppressor (deletion_coupled). cis_dosage_class cannot: PTEN, RB1, CDKN2A and ERBB2 all read coupled. Populated only for coupled_* classes, so it never fires alongside cn_dosage_uncoupled.

cis_dosage_direction is a RANKING of the two arms, not an independent significance claim. With cis_dosage_direction_basis=cn_distribution_asymmetry neither arm was powered or above the magnitude floor and the direction is read off the CN distribution's longer tail — weak evidence, so read the arm deltas rather than quoting the direction alone.

The focal-amplification subset escape is lineage-CONTROLLED (v1.1.0): the amplified group must over-express relative to NEUTRAL LINES OF THE SAME LINEAGE, not just the panel. Without that control a lineage-restricted gene passes on lineage separation alone (CDH1: +3.26 log2TPM pan-panel, -0.70 within lineage). subset_within_lineage_delta_log2tpm and subset_n_lineages_compared are the audit trail; subset_n_lineages_compared=0 means no lineage was jointly powered and the escape is withheld.

Cell-line cis-dosage is necessary but NOT sufficient for a patient cis-driver claim — it needs orthogonal patient validation, now provided by the sibling patient-cis-coherence card (patient CN↔expression join at the case barcode via tcga-sample-id-crosswalk-v1, R4). ERBB2/BRCA and CDKN2A/HNSC replicate the cell-line coupling in patient tumours (live).

clingen-dosage.question: Is loss of one copy of {target.symbol} pathogenic (ClinGen autosomal-dominant / haploinsufficiency), implying a dosage-sensitivity safety concern for a full-KO modality — and what is the germline INHERITANCE MODE (recessive-only = carriers healthy = full-KO reassurance)?

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol}: ClinGen autosomal-dominant loss is pathogenic ({top_disease}, {top_confidence}) — single-copy loss suffices for disease (haploinsufficiency), a safety concern for full-KO modalities (degrader/RNA/full SM). Mutant-selective tx vs an activating driver spares WT, nullifying this.

caveats:
ClinGen carries no dosage column; dosage_sensitivity_class is DERIVED from allelicRequirements
(AD → dominant-loss, AR → dosage-sufficient) gated on confidence (Definitive/Strong only —
Disputed/Refuted excluded). A gene can be both AD and AR across diseases (BRCA1, MLH1); the card
reports autosomal_dominant_loss whenever ANY high-confidence dominant association exists, because
single-copy loss is then pathogenic for at least that disease.
This is a germline gene-disease-validity signal about the WILD-TYPE gene's dosage sensitivity. It
does not capture adult-vs-developmental requirements (cross-reference mouse-ko-phenotype), and a
mutant-selective therapy against an activating driver spares WT and largely nullifies the concern
(resolver mechanism-conditioning downgrade).
germline_inheritance_mode is the in-hand OMIM-style inheritance signal (same ClinGen
allelicRequirements — no OMIM license). recessive_only = a strictly-recessive-disease gene whose
heterozygous carriers are healthy → a POSITIVE full-KO reassurance the dominant-focused
dosage_sensitivity_class understates (it collapses recessive → dosage_sufficient). ADDITIVE /
verdict-inert: fires no rule; the safety verdict still rests on dominant-loss + constraint + mouse-KO.
Deferred, license/cross-release-gated follow-ups for a richer human-KO safety picture: direct OMIM
morbidmap ingestion (finer phenotype-severity + full inheritance beyond ClinGen's curated set) and
gnomAD-v2 obs_hom_lof (observed healthy human knockouts). The ClinGen-derived inheritance mode here
covers the non-redundant inheritance-axis value without either gate.

emitted ONLY when both target and partner are on ALL GENIE panels
contributing to the pooled cohort. Genes outside the intersect get
per-source Q-values only. Every emitted row carries `pooled_eligible`

"not sequenced in GENIE" as "not co-mutated") is prevented by this
filter.

covered partners). Not multiplicity across all possible target-partner
combinations in the genome.

copy-number-distribution.question: Across DepMap cell lines, what is the copy-number landscape for {target.symbol}? Is the target recurrently amplified, deleted, or broadly neutral?

figures.description: Pan-cancer CN distribution with KDE overlay. Threshold reference lines at deletion (0.92) and amplification (1.5). Tight distribution near 1.0 = broadly neutral; long left tail = recurrent deletion; long right tail = recurrent amplification.
Per-lineage CN strip plot, lineages ordered by median CN descending (n≥5 only). Identifies lineage-specific amplification or deletion (e.g., MYC amp in HCC, NF1 deletion in NF1-syndrome lines).
Per-cell-line CN sorted ascending. Preserves per-line resolution that density bins out; secondary view.

warning_predicates.message: WES CN panel has missing scores for many cell lines — interpretation may be biased toward the captured subset.
Amplification tail is essentially one-lineage-driven; pan-cancer 'recurrently_amplified' label may be misleading.
Deletion tail is essentially one-lineage-driven; pan-cancer 'recurrently_deleted' label may be misleading.

caveats: copy_number_class == recurrently_deleted does NOT establish a target-specific deletion. The score is shallow-inclusive and clears its 0.20 cut for 60.1% of ALL genes genome-wide (median gene 0.228, ABOVE the cut), vs 2.9% for the amplification arm and 1.5% for the deep-deletion fraction (measured 2026-09-12, 1433 sampled genes). It reads the aneuploid cell-line background, not target-specific loss.

Because of that 60.1% null rate, the genomic resolver (>= 1.9.0) fires NO driver-establishing rung on recurrently_deleted — treat it as a DISPLAY/modality read. A deletion DRIVER claim keys on cn_homozygous_deletion_recurrent (biallelic, 1.5% null) or patient_focal_cn_class (indication-native GISTIC -2). The amplification arm is unaffected (2.9% null, no measured defect).
Most cancer driver genes (KRAS, BRAF, EGFR, etc.) are MUTATION-driven, not CN-driven. A 'broadly_neutral' call is the correct, expected outcome for these — NOT a coverage gap.

Method uses WES gene-level CN (OmicsCNGeneMC_WES.csv, n≈1954) as PRIMARY. When the target gene is absent from the WES panel (e.g. MYC, BRAF in 26Q1), method falls back to WGS gene-level CN (OmicsCNGeneWGS.csv, n≈800, full genome coverage). Card emits cn_assay_used ∈ {wes, wgs} to surface which source was used per target. Different denominators per target are honest reporting, not silent imputation.
CN scale is raw relative CN (median ~1.0 = diploid), NOT log2 ratio. Thresholds: deep del < 0.5, shallow del < 0.92, neutral 0.92-1.07, shallow amp >1.07, focal amp >1.5, high amp >4.

Copy number ≠ functional effect: a focal amplification can be passenger; a homozygous deletion of a tumor-suppressor can be a driver. Functional inference requires the dependency cards as orthogonal evidence.

TWO CN COHORTS, CONSENSUS VERDICT: copy_number_class is DepMap CELL-LINE CN; the patient_* fields are TCGA PATIENT-tumour GISTIC (tcga-patient-cn-per-gene-v1, per-INDICATION). The genomic CN-driver verdict rung fires on EITHER cell-line recurrent amp/del OR patient FOCAL amp/del (cell-line-OR-patient consensus) — strictly ADDITIVE: it only RESCUES false-negatives (e.g. ERBB2/BRCA, cell-line-neutral but patient-focal-amplified), never weakens an existing cell-line call.

The patient VERDICT gate is patient_focal_cn_class (HIGH-LEVEL +2 amp / -2 homdel only) — NOT patient_copy_number_class, which fires on any-gain (>= +1, includes arm-level noise like KRAS 12p) and stays a DISPLAY cross-check. This focal gate keeps arm-level gain out of the verdict. Patient CN uses raw GISTIC discrete (honest amp+del), NOT the LoF-biased 'min-wins' two-hit product.

The two CN cohorts can legitimately DIFFER (cell-line = pan-cancer + culture-selected; patient = indication-specific, in-vivo). A gene amplified in patients but not the cell-line panel — or the reverse — is a decision-useful discrepancy to surface, not an error. patient_high_amp_fraction (GISTIC +2) is the cleaner focal-oncogene signal vs patient_amplified_fraction (any gain, includes arm-level).

copy-number-stratified-dependency.question: Is dependency on {target.symbol} stratified by {target.symbol}'s own copy-number amplification status across the DepMap panel? (Amplification-addiction biomarker hypothesis.)

figures.description: Per-cell-line Chronos strip plot split into Amplified (relative CN > 2.0) / Neutral groups. Reference lines at Chronos = -1.0 + 0. Annotated with the q-value + delta.

warning_predicates.message: Fewer than 10 amplified cell lines; amplification-stratification estimate has wide CI. Interpret cn_stratification_class cautiously.

Amplified-vs-neutral difference is statistically significant but sub-threshold in effect size (delta > -0.2) — at panel n, small deltas reach significance; not classified as stratified (significance != actionable effect).

caveats: Amplification status = DepMap relative copy number > 2.0 (focal HIGH-LEVEL amp convention; diploid ~ 1.0, NOT log2). Does not distinguish focal from arm-level/broad amplification.

Two directional passes: a FORWARD one-sided MW (amplified more dependent) drives the amplified_*_dependent classes; a SECOND-PASS reverse MW (neutral more dependent) makes `neutral_strongly_dependent` reachable, gated on its own BH q + a strong positive delta (>= +0.5). Amplification is never credited with a dependency it lacks (forward classes cannot fire on a reverse pattern); the reverse class is verdict-inert.

Amplification and mutation stratification are NOT independent — an amplified target is often also mutant/co-selected (e.g. KRAS). When both stratify, the resolver's mutation rung takes precedence (driving_rule names the mutation path).
Cell-line amplification-stratified dependency is necessary but NOT sufficient for a clinical biomarker — needs orthogonal validation (PDX, isogenic, patient copy-number).

Strict 'is the target amplified' boolean at a single relative-CN cutoff — does not model amplicon structure, co-amplified neighbours, or expression consequence. Those are downstream questions (see the amp→expression→dependency three-way signature).

CRISPR and RNAi disagree substantially. Treat single-assay dependency claims with caution; consider partial-knockdown vs knockout-saturation explanations.

caveats: Concordance is computed ONLY on cell lines measured in BOTH assays. Single-assay lines are reported in their provenance buckets (n_crispr_only_*, n_rnai_only_*) but never imputed.

degradation-feasibility.question: Is {target.symbol} a tractable degradation substrate — does E3-substrate biology, degrader precedent, and subcellular location support a PROTAC / molecular-glue program?

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} is a surface/secreted protein — outside cytoplasmic-E3 reach, so a classic intracellular PROTAC/molecular-glue cannot degrade it. A biologics surface modality (ADC/TCE) applies instead; do not read a degrader rationale here.
{target.symbol} has no E3-substrate, precedent, or location signal — degradation feasibility is UNKNOWN (a coverage gap), not 'infeasible'.

caveats:
Degrader-lens E3 slice: this card fills the degradability_machinery slot the
tractability-small-molecule degrader lens reported as not_yet_assessed. It reasons about whether
the TARGET is a tractable degradation substrate — NOT whether the degradation machinery (CRBN/VHL/
proteasome) is expressed in a given lineage (those E3s are near-ubiquitous; expression adds little
discrimination and is deliberately not the signal).
ASYMMETRY (do not misread absence): only unfavorable_location is a true negative. Absence of a
natural E3 substrate is NOT disqualifying — PROTACs create INDUCED neo-substrate relationships
(recruit any E3), so an intracellular target with no UbiBrowser evidence reads plausible_untested,
never infeasible. Natural-substrate presence is a POSITIVE prior (ubiquitination-competent), not a
requirement.
Precedent > substrate. precedented_degradable comes from the curated
degrader_precedent_targets.yaml (targets with a named clinical/tool degrader). Because PROTAC-DB is
license-restricted (no mirroring), precedent is captured as curated facts citing it + primary
literature, NOT by ingesting PROTAC-DB. Coverage is intentionally small/high-precision and grows
manually.
Natural E3-substrate evidence is from UbiBrowser (ubibrowser-e3-substrate-per-gene-v1): literature
= manually PubMed-curated; predicted_only = ML-predicted (Pvalue<=0.05) with no curated pair. The
location gate uses surfaceome-family-classification (surface/secreted vs intracellular). HGNC
symbol keys throughout. UbiBrowser open-with-citation (Li 2017 Nat Commun + Wang 2022 NAR).

dependency-lineage-selectivity.question: Across all DepMap lineages, how does {target.symbol} dependency stratify? Which lineages are enriched for dependence?

figures.description: Per-lineage Chronos median (point) + IQR (horizontal bar) across ALL lineages with n ≥ min. Sorted by median ascending. Reference at Chronos = -1.0 (strong) and 0 (no dependency). Indication-lineage highlighting applied at render time by the synthesis layer.
Per-lineage strip plot of individual cell-line Chronos points. Distribution within each lineage visible (informs IQR confidence).

warning_predicates.message: Fewer than 10 lineages with sufficient sample size for the enrichment test. Lineage-selectivity classification is less robust on small lineage counts.

Three or more lineages are significantly enriched for dependency. Indication selection requires comparing the enriched lineages directly; the most-enriched lineage may not be the canonical clinical indication.

caveats: Chronos scores reflect cell-line dependency; in-vivo dependency may differ due to tumor microenvironment, vasculature, immune context.
Enrichment test compares each lineage's Chronos distribution against the rest of the panel via Mann-Whitney U; BH multiple-testing correction across all evaluated lineages.
Small lineages (n < 10) excluded from the enrichment test; their stats appear in per_lineage_stats but cannot be ranked for enrichment.
Lineage-specificity does not preclude expansion to adjacent lineages with similar dependency — consult per_lineage_stats for adjacency.
DepMap lineage assignments are based on OncotreeLineage; some cancer types may have ambiguous lineage classification.

Enrichment is RELATIVE; admission to enriched_lineages additionally requires reaching modest_dependency_chronos at the finest adequately-powered grain (lineage, else a constituent OncotreeCode). Lineages passing the relative test alone are disclosed on relative_only_enriched_lineages and do NOT drive enrichment_class.

enrichment_class is a PANEL-SHAPE label and is NOT indication-conditioned: it says a lineage somewhere is enriched, never that the queried one is. Read indication_dependency_class for the queried indication. Therapeutic interpretation of both lives in interpretation-rules/.

indication_dependency_class is a READ-SIDE reduction of the fields above over the indication's depmap_oncotree_codes (indication_crosswalk), not a new measurement — the method takes no indication argument. It is written by the dependency card preprocessor; on a target-grain run it is indication_not_supplied, which means the question was not asked and is NOT a data gap.

warning_predicates.message: Predictability fit used fewer than 200 cell lines — R² estimate has higher variance; interpret class call with caution.
95% CI on r² spans more than 0.20 — high uncertainty; a single-run r² point estimate over-states confidence in the biomarker class call.

RF and XGBoost disagree on r² by more than 0.10 — feature-attribution structure differs between tree types. Inspect the top_features_xgb list; a divergent XGBoost identifies an interaction structure RF misses.
Lineage one-hot dominates; the model has essentially learned a per-lineage baseline. Patient-selection beyond indication unlikely from standard omics.

caveats: v2 approximates DepMap Daintree's transform_driver_events (which uses OncoKB's auth-gated per-variant Oncogenic + MutationEffect annotations) with a coarser GENE-ROLE join (OncoKB public gene list × DepMap hotspot/damaging matrices). This means some GoF/LoF flags may be less specific than DepMap's — particularly for genes where OncoKB's per-variant curation resolves ambiguous mutations.

cross_gene_expression + cross_gene_copy_number features fill NaNs with 0 / 1.0 (diploid) respectively rather than dropping rows. This preserves the ~1500-cell CRISPR panel but introduces some noise on the discarded features. SelectKBest inside each CV fold retains only the 1000 most-informative features (per-fold, no leakage) so noise on the discarded features is soft-capped.

predictability_class is DESCRIPTIVE — `unpredictable` means standard features don't explain Chronos, NOT that the dependency is artefactual. Pair with E1/E2 to confirm the dependency itself is real before discounting.

Bootstrap CI on r² is over cell-line indices at the OOF-prediction level. It does NOT propagate uncertainty from feature-selection (KBest inside folds) or hyperparameter choice. A tighter CI would nest bootstrap around the full CV loop — infeasible at ~18k-gene scale.

Own driver flags (driver_{target}_GoF / driver_{target}_LoF) are EXCLUDED from the OncoKB flag feature block for each target — same feature as own_mut_hotspot / own_mut_damaging; would leak label information. Cross-driver flags (driver_TP53_LoF when target=KRAS, etc.) are retained since they capture co-driver context.

functional-gene-state.question: Is {target.symbol} biallelically inactivated (completed two-hit) or only monoallelically hit in {indication.label} — and by what mechanism (mutation, copy loss, LOH, homozygous deletion)?
caveats: EPIGENETIC second hit is DETECTED: promoter hypermethylation (e.g. MLH1/BRCA1/VHL/CDKN2A) upgrades wt→epigenetic and monoallelic→biallelic+epigenetic. Sources: patient GDC-SeSAMe HM450 (tcga-sesame-promoter-methylation-v1; cohorts LUAD/LUSC/HNSC/PAAD/STAD/ESCA) + model CCLE RRBS. EPIC not ingested; an indication without a landed methylation cohort degrades to the genetic-only states (no false downgrade).

PATIENT arm is the SHARP arm: PanCanAtlas ABSOLUTE gives PER-LOCUS allele-specific LOH (point-in-interval at the mutation locus), so copy-neutral LOH biallelic events are resolved cleanly. MODEL arm has only DepMap RELATIVE per-gene CN + GENOME-WIDE LoH, so copy-neutral per-gene LOH is undeterminable → those cell lines resolve `uncertain` rather than a false biallelic. The arms agree on mechanism but the patient arm is more sensitive to copy-neutral two-hit events.

`uncertain` means a mutation is present but the second-hit background could not be confirmed (CN/LOH not measured) — it is NOT `wt`. It is EXCLUDED from the fraction_biallelic denominator (undeterminable, not not-biallelic) but COUNTED in fraction_any_alteration (the sample does carry a hit).

gene-level, not variant-resolved: a passenger mutation co-occurring with LOH is scored as a two-hit event even if the specific variant is functionally neutral. Interpret alongside alteration-role (is the gene an LoF driver at all?).

patient CN homdel uses GISTIC discrete −2 (per-gene); patient LOH uses ABSOLUTE segments (point-in-interval). Both hg19, build-consistent with the hg19 MC3 MAF — no cross-build gene-coordinate lookup.

caveats: Consensus of 3 TCGA callers (TumorFusions/Hu 2018 PRADA, Gao 2018, cBioPortal PanCancer Atlas 2018 SV), UNIONED not intersected — caller_count in the product encodes agreement; the reader's min_callers arg (1=union default / 2=majority) lets a consumer require consensus.

Driver-fusion counts are SMALL per tissue (e.g. ~5 ALK in LUAD) — a RECURRENCE/landscape signal, not a per-patient diagnostic. fusion_frequency is n_samples_with_fusion / assayed samples in the indication tissue (sample_coverage), or None when the coverage denominator is unavailable — never a rate over an unknown cohort.

The TCGA-consensus facts are DEEP but tissue-limited (33 TCGA types). fusion-stratified-dependency.question: Is dependency on {target.symbol} stratified by whether the cell line carries a fusion involving {target.symbol} across the DepMap panel? (Fusion-addiction biomarker hypothesis.)

figures.description: Per-cell-line Chronos strip plot split into Fusion-positive (target is a partner) / Fusion-negative groups. Reference lines at Chronos = -1.0 + 0. Annotated with the q-value + delta.

warning_predicates.message: Fewer than 10 fusion-positive cell lines; fusion-stratification estimate has wide CI. Interpret fusion_stratification_class cautiously.

Fusion-positive-vs-negative difference is statistically significant but sub-threshold in effect size (delta > -0.2) — at panel n, small deltas reach significance; not classified as stratified (significance != actionable effect).

caveats: Fusion status = the target appears as EITHER the 5' (LeftGene) or 3' (RightGene) partner in any default high-confidence DepMap fusion call (gene-collapsed symbol-union boolean). v1 does NOT require the target be the in-frame / kinase-retaining / dependency-conferring partner — 5'/3' orientation + reading-frame resolution (OmicsFusionFilteredSupplementary) is a v2 upgrade.

The symbol-union v1 is CONSERVATIVE by construction: the one-sided Mann-Whitney (alternative: fusion-positive more dependent) means a bystander-partner fusion (target is the passenger fragment) only dilutes toward the null — it can never manufacture a false-positive dependency call.

Fusion-negative comparator = every OTHER fusion-PROFILED line. Lines absent from OmicsFusionFiltered.csv were never fusion-called and are EXCLUDED (abstain), not counted as negatives — the denominator is the profiled universe, not all Chronos-screened lines.

Two directional passes: a FORWARD one-sided MW (fusion-positive more dependent) drives the fusion_positive_*_dependent classes; a SECOND-PASS reverse MW (fusion-negative more dependent) makes `fusion_negative_strongly_dependent` reachable, gated on its own BH q + a strong positive delta (>= +0.5). A fusion is never credited with a dependency it lacks (forward classes cannot fire on a reverse pattern); the reverse class is verdict-inert.

Fusion, mutation, and copy-number stratification are NOT independent. When more than one stratifies, the resolver's mutation rung takes precedence, then CN, then fusion (driving_rule names the winning path).

Cell-line fusion-stratified dependency is necessary but NOT sufficient for a clinical biomarker — needs orthogonal validation (fusion-positive PDX, isogenic breakpoint constructs, patient fusion status).

gene-burden-safety.question: Does population rare-variant burden (Open Targets) show that loss of {target.symbol} function is harmful (a WT-loss safety signal) or protective?

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol}: LoF variants INCREASE disease risk (OT burden, p={min_pvalue}, {top_disease}) — loss of function is harmful at population scale, an on-target safety risk for full-KO modalities (degrader/RNA/full SM). Mutant-selective tx vs an activating driver spares WT, nullifying this.

{target.symbol} rare-variant burden shows LoF variants are PROTECTIVE against disease (Open Targets, top trait: {top_disease}). Loss of function is beneficial at population scale — a drug-POSITIVE human-genetics signal, not a safety concern.

caveats:
Burden evidence is uniformly LoF-on-target in OT 26.06, so the risk/protect DIRECTION comes from
directionOnTrait (whether LoF raises or lowers disease risk), not directionOnTarget. A
`direction_unresolved` call means the gene carries BOTH significant risk AND protective burden
associations across different traits (405 genes do) — the card declines a one-directional safety
call rather than fire a false hold.
This is GERMLINE population genetics — a WT-loss-tolerance signal. It does NOT capture
tissue-specific or adult-vs-developmental requirements (cross-reference mouse-ko-phenotype
for the developmental-vs-adult distinction), and it is about the WILD-TYPE protein: a
mutant-selective therapy against an activating driver spares WT and largely nullifies this
concern (the resolver's mechanism-conditioning downgrade).
Significance is gated at p < 1e-6 on the OT-composed p-value (mantissa × 10^exponent). `beta` is
frequently null in OT burden evidence, so effect DIRECTION rests on directionOnTrait, with beta
corroborating only where present.

genomic-event-model-match.question: Which DepMap models carry the same functional genomic event in {target.symbol} as {indication.label} tumors, and which of those genotype-matched models are dependent (positive screen lines)?

warning_predicates.message: Fewer than 5 genotype-matched DepMap models carry the tumor's functional event. An event_matched_not_dependent call rests on a small matched set — absence of dependency across few matched models is weak evidence of non-dependency. Read alongside the pan-cancer and lineage dependency cards.

caveats: GENOTYPE-identity correspondence, NOT expression-similarity (recommended-models) and NOT full-transcriptome Celligner. The two patient↔model joins are complementary — a model can match on one axis and mismatch on the other; that disagreement is the signal (expression-matched but genotype-mismatched = poor model for a LoF-driven dependency).

The tumor EVENT matched is the dominant ALTERED state (biallelic-genetic preferred over monoallelic; ≥10% of tumors). When tumors are rarely altered there is no recurrent genotype to match → event_correspondence_class = no_target_event (an honest 'no target event', not forced to wild-type).

Model genotype inherits functional-gene-state's model-arm caveat: DepMap has relative per-gene CN + genome-wide LoH only, so copy-neutral per-gene LOH resolves `uncertain` (not biallelic). A model that is truly copy-neutral-LOH biallelic may read `uncertain` and miss an event_match — a false-negative-leaning bias, documented.
event_match is STRICT genotype identity on the dominant event; a model with a DIFFERENT alteration (e.g. monoallelic where the tumor is biallelic) is not counted as matched even though it is altered.
Chronos is pan-lineage per-model dependency; a positive_model is genotype-matched + dependent but the dependency may be context-driven. Screen role is a starting panel, not a validated model set.

caveats: INDICATION-LEVEL + target-INDEPENDENT: aneuploidy + WGD are genome-wide cohort phenotypes, not per-gene calls. The classes describe the indication's chromosomal instability / doubling prevalence, not the target — a target's own copy-number is copy-number-distribution; its two-hit state is functional-gene-state.

Per-SAMPLE genome-wide instability (frac_altered), NOT per-arm. A per-arm arm-loss / per-lineage-selectivity-percentile view needs Taylor-2018 arm-level calls (not yet ingested) — deferred. DISPLAY facet, verdict-inert.

WGD prevalence (wgd_class / wgd_fraction) is from PanCanAtlas ABSOLUTE Genome-doublings (>=1 doubling), the sibling of the aneuploidy burden — the two axes correlate (WGD-enriched cohorts run higher frac_altered + ploidy) but are reported separately. High WGD is a copy-number-noise + prognosis caveat, NOT a target-specific amplification signal.

PATIENT MSI (msi_class / msi_high_fraction) is from TCGA marker-paper labels, CRC + STAD ONLY — other indications return data_unavailable (UNLABELLED, NOT a measured 0% MSI-high). The MODEL arm (model_msi_class, DepMap MSIsensor) FILLS this gap: all-lineage, so NSCLC/PAAD get a measured model_msi_class where patient msi_class is unavailable. A genome-wide PATIENT MSIsensor score is a deferred derivation. Cohort-level, target-independent.

MODEL MSI (model_msi_class / model_msi_high_fraction) is DepMap cell-line MSIsensor (MSIScore >= 20 = MSI-H), a MODEL-cohort property — NOT patient prevalence (MSI-H lines are over-represented vs tumours, so model fractions can run higher). DepMap 26q1 merges gastric with esophageal into 'Esophagus/Stomach', so GC/STAD/ESCA model MSI is broader than gastric alone (dilutes vs the patient STAD label). Where both arms exist they cross-validate; where they differ, note the cohort difference.

MODEL MMR-SIGNATURE (model_mmr_signature_class) is DepMap SBS exposures normalized per-model; MMR-deficiency signatures (SBS6/14/15/20/21/26/44) are an INDEPENDENT cross-validation of the MSI axis — a different signal (mutation spectrum, not microsatellite length) that tracks it closely (uterus/bowel enriched, lung rare). Reported as the FRACTION of lines MMR-sig-high (a subset phenomenon; the cohort median sits at MSS baseline).

model_hrd_signature_present_fraction (SBS3, defective-HR) is a WEAK PARP-sensitivity proxy ONLY: SBS3 is flat/featureless and rarely dominates a cell line's spectrum, so a low 10% presence threshold is used and near-zero fractions are expected. A real HRD / genomic-scar score (scarHRD-style, allele-specific CN) is a deferred derivation. Do NOT read a low HRD-signature fraction as HR-proficient.

gnomad-lof-constraint.question: How constrained is {target.symbol} against loss-of-function variants in the gnomAD population, and what does this imply for on-target safety?

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} is highly LoF-constrained in gnomAD (pli>=0.9 or loeuf<=0.45). Population evidence suggests LoF is not tolerated — on-target safety risk if the therapy fully abrogates protein function. Consider partial-agonism, allosteric, or dose-controlled strategies vs full-KO modalities.
Synonymous Z-score is an outlier — the constraint calibration may be unreliable for {target.symbol}. Interpret pli + loeuf cautiously.
{target.symbol} is not in the gnomAD constraint table (possibly on non-canonical chromosomes, or excluded by quality filters). No germline LoF-tolerance signal available.

caveats:
pLI (probability of LoF-intolerance) and LOEUF (loss-of-function
observed/expected upper fraction) are gnomAD's canonical constraint
metrics. Highly-constrained genes (pLI >= 0.9) are enriched for
haploinsufficiency + developmental disorders — a therapy that fully
abrogates function may recapitulate the disease phenotype systemically.
Constraint signals are BULK-POPULATION averages; they do NOT capture
tissue-specific or age-specific requirements. A gene that is constrained
at the germline / developmental level may be dispensable in adult
tissues (e.g. hedgehog pathway components tolerated post-development).
Governance readers should cross-reference IMPC mouse-KO phenotypes
for tissue-specific requirements.
LOEUF is preferred over pLI for confidence intervals — pLI is a binary-
ish score whereas LOEUF encodes uncertainty directly. Recent literature
(Karczewski et al 2020) recommends LOEUF as the primary constraint
metric.
Constraint does NOT preclude therapeutic development — many well-
validated oncology targets (e.g. TP53) are highly constrained. The
signal informs modality choice + safety monitoring, not go/no-go.
Future upgrades: pair with IMPC mouse KO phenotypes (tissue-specific
lethality), ClinVar germline (population variant health outcomes),
OMIM disease associations (autosomal dominant / recessive contexts).
All three are expansions beyond this card.
human_ko_observed_class complements constraint_class with DIRECT observation: obs_hom_lof
counts healthy individuals HOMOZYGOUS for a predicted-LoF variant (natural human knockouts).
`natural_ko_observed` (obs_hom_lof>=1) is strong safety reassurance for a full-KO modality.
Sourced from gnomAD v2.1.1 (~125k genomes) joined by gene symbol onto the v4.1.1 row — a
deliberate cross-release choice (v2.1.1 is the standard hom-KO reference; v4 omits it).
ASYMMETRY (do not misread a zero): observing a natural KO is meaningful, but its ABSENCE
is weak — homozygous LoF is rare in 125k people (only ~12% of genes have any), so
obs_hom_lof=0 does NOT imply essentiality. That inference belongs to pLI/LOEUF:
`constrained_no_ko` = zero + constrained (essentiality from the constraint), `no_natural_ko`
= zero + tolerant (uninformative), `data_unavailable` = absent from the v2 join (not zero).

immune-context.question: For {indication.label}, is the tumor immune-hot or immune-cold — is there a CD8 T-cell effector population present for a T-cell engager to redirect?

warning_predicates.message: {indication.label} is immune-COLD (CD8 fraction <= pan-cancer 25th pctile). A T-cell engager needs an effector pool to redirect — a T-cell-excluded tumor is a first-order TCE efficacy risk however clean the antigen. Consider TME-conditioning combos or an ADC (T-cell-independent payload).

caveats:
The PRIMARY call is target-INDEPENDENT: the immune landscape of the INDICATION, not conditioned on
the target antigen. The sharper question — are the ANTIGEN-HIGH patients also T-cell-high? — is
answered by the additive antigen-conditioned facet, which is verdict-INERT and degrades to
data_unavailable on a thin barcode join. Read the primary class as the baseline effector context for
the indication, not a per-target claim.
THE CLASS IS A PAN-CANCER RANK, NOT AN ABSOLUTE DENSITY. The cuts ARE the 33-study Q3 (0.113) and Q1
(0.084), so ~a quarter of studies are hot and a quarter cold BY CONSTRUCTION — the token says where the
indication ranks among cancers, not that there are enough T cells. Clinically-cold PRAD (0.1312) reads
hot; ICI-APPROVED BLCA (0.1103) and LUAD (0.0876) read intermediate. Show the frame (share, LEUKOCYTE
denominator, n_samples, both cuts) beside the token.
DENOMINATOR CEILING (hematologic / lymphoid cohorts). LM22 reports the CD8 share OF THE LEUKOCYTE
COMPARTMENT, so in a leukemia, lymphoma or lymphoid organ the denominator IS the malignant clone —
arithmetically valid, biologically meaningless, yet confidently classed (LAML 0.0216, DLBC 0.1142,
THYM 0.2782). Those three now RESOLVE and are answered by `lymphoid_denominator_unreliable`, which
WITHHOLDS the median — on TCE-validated DLBCL, "a cohort exists but its frame does not apply".
CIBERSORT LM22 gives RELATIVE leukocyte fractions (composition of the immune compartment), not
absolute infiltrate density. A high CD8 FRACTION in a lymphocyte-poor tumor is fewer absolute CD8
cells than the same fraction in a lymphocyte-rich tumor. The class is a relative-composition screen;
pair with an absolute-infiltrate or IHC read before a hard immune-cold call.
Bulk deconvolution (CIBERSORT on bulk RNA-seq) estimates composition; it does not resolve spatial
exclusion (T cells present but stroma-restricted, not tumor-infiltrating). Spatial / single-cell
confirms whether CD8 cells actually contact tumor cells — a documented next layer.

INDIRECT modulators. So a structurally 'hard' target (e.g. TP53) can carry many interactions
(p53-reactivators, indirect modulators). Read the class WITH the structure leg, not instead of
it — the two legs measure different things and a rich interaction count is not a pocket.
Absence is a COVERAGE GAP, never undruggability (measured-vs-null discipline). no_known_drug_evidence
means the gene is not in DGIdb, not that it cannot be drugged. approved_drug_tractable is hoisted
above clinically_actionable (an approved drug is the harder pharmacology fact).
MODALITY (v1.2.0, CASE-008): has_approved_drug is modality-BLIND. A biologics-only antigen (approved
ADC/TCE/CAR/mAb, no approved SM; biologics_precedent_targets.yaml biologics_only: true) resolves
approved_drug_engagement_class=approved_biologic_only, gating off the SM-supportive approved-drug rung.
Fail-safe: dual-modality SM targets (EGFR/ERBB2/MET) + FOLH1/PSMA carry no flag → never demoted
(osimertinib guard); absence of the flag = prior behaviour.
STALENESS: the DGIdb source (dgidb-2026-06b) self-reports Data version Dec-2023 / DGIdb v5.0.11
despite the 2026 release tag — a repackaging, not fresh curation. Treat the drug-gene + category
content as a Dec-2023 snapshot. Cite Cannon et al. 2024 NAR (DGIdb 5.0).

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} is absent from both ChEMBL-bioactivity and BindingDB. This is a COVERAGE GAP — not evidence that no chemical matter exists. Check the structure leg (structure-features-static) for a forward-ligandability handle.

caveats:
Measured-potency leg (ChEMBL + BindingDB) of small-molecule tractability. Answers "is there a
POTENT measured ligand + how deep is the series" — the MEASURED-binding complement to the
structure leg (a druggable pocket), the retrospective PRISM leg (cell-line killing), and the
DGIdb known-drug leg (presence, not potency). A target can have potent measured chemical matter
WITHOUT a clean predicted pocket (or vice versa) — read the legs together.
CALIBRATION: a SINGLE potent activity (best_pchembl >= 6) is near-universal for studied genes, so
the strong `potent_measured_ligand` verdict requires a potent-ligand SERIES (>= 10 potent ligands),
a chemotype depth signal — not one reported binder. n_potent_ligands is the discriminating field;
best_pchembl alone is display context.

stays the distinct measured-POTENCY dimension; the phase class is an orthogonal clinical-precedent leg.
Absence is a COVERAGE GAP, never 'undruggable' (measured-vs-null discipline). data_unavailable means
the gene is in neither bioactivity source. LICENSE: ChEMBL is CC-BY-SA-3.0 (share-alike); this leg
consumes ONLY the aggregate rollup (potent-ligand counts + best-potency maxima), not raw activity
rows. Cite ChEMBL (Zdrazil et al. 2024 NAR) + BindingDB (Gilson et al. 2016 NAR).

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol}'s tumor-dominant exon {best_exon_id} stands {exon_heterogeneity_log2} log2 above the gene-median exon with a {best_exon_window_ratio}x window — a HYPOTHESIS worth junction/isoform-resolved follow-up. {target.symbol}'s tumor-dominant exon is also expressed in an essential normal organ above the modality tier — even at exon resolution the window is not clean for this modality.

caveats:
HYPOTHESIS-GENERATING, not isoform-identity (load-bearing): per-exon COVERAGE quantiles

isoform (it cannot resolve CLDN18.2 from CLDN18.1). Isoform identity needs junction/PSI data.

isoforms (MET-ex14, EGFRvIII — the ABSENCE of an exon, a signal this card cannot see).
RNA, not protein. Exon-level TPM is a transcript-inclusion proxy; it does not prove the isoform
is translated or the epitope is displayed on the tumor cell surface.

modality-therapeutic-window.question: For {target.symbol} in {indication.label}, is tumor expression high enough relative to the worst essential normal organ to open a therapeutic window for a biologic at each modality tier (strict TCE / moderate ADC / pathway antibody)?

warning_predicates.message: Essential-only window looks clean, but a NON-ESSENTIAL normal tissue ({max_full_normal_organ}, {max_full_normal_tpm} TPM) exceeds tumor — the essential-only blind spot (TACSTD2/TROP2, high in skin/salivary). An ADC may tolerate this; a strict TCE typically cannot.

{target.symbol} tumor median < 1.0 TPM in the {indication.label} TCGA cohort — window call cannot be made here. If the target's true indication lacks a TCGA study (e.g. DLL3/SCLC), this is a cohort artifact, not a biological absence.

caveats:
CROSS-SOURCE BATCH CONFOUND (first-order): the numerator (TCGA tumor) and denominator (GTEx
normal) are different assays harmonized onto one recount3/GENCODE-v26 TPM axis, NOT a matched
tumor-vs-adjacent contrast — a raw ratio inherits residual batch effects. Read the window as a
MODALITY-TIER SCREEN (does an essential organ trip the threshold?); cross-check the magnitude
against the within-cohort tumor-vs-normal-selectivity card before citing a specific fold-value.
ESSENTIAL vs FULL-NORMAL denominators are BOTH emitted deliberately. window_ratio_essential
drives the modality-tier liability call (the biologics repo's core signal); window_ratio_full_normal
is the Theme-1 correction — the source scorer discarded the full-normal max and thereby understated
dirtiness for antigens whose liability is a NON-essential tissue (TACSTD2 skin/salivary, CEACAM5
colon). When the two diverge, the full-normal ratio is the more conservative read for a strict TCE.
The window is TCGA-cohort-based. Indications without a TCGA study resolve data_unavailable (never a
silent coarser fall-back). Tumor numerator = MAX median across the indication's TCGA studies
(COADREAD = max over COAD, READ) — the study where the target is highest gets its due.
RNA, not protein. TPM is a transcript proxy; a surface antigen's deliverable target is the PROTEIN.
Pair with surface-abundance-density (copies/cell) + protein-surface-evidence (CSPA) for the
protein-reality half of a biologics decision. The window is an efficacy/safety-SCREEN axis.

mouse-ko-phenotype.question: Does mouse knockout of {target.symbol} cause ADULT lethality or severe organ dysfunction (a normal-physiology safety signal), as distinct from purely developmental lethality?

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol}: mouse ADULT/postnatal knockout is lethal ({top_lethal_label}) — an adult-essential-function signal (inferred, mouse model), an on-target safety caution for full-KO modalities. Mouse KO is a MODEL not a human measurement; mutant-selective tx vs an activating driver spares WT.

{target.symbol}: mouse knockout is lethal only at developmental stages ({top_lethal_label}), NOT postnatally. This reflects an EMBRYONIC role and does NOT establish adult on-target toxicity — many developmentally-essential genes are dispensable in adult tissue. Context, not a safety hold.

caveats:
Mouse KO is a MODEL of human physiology (evidence_tier: inferred) — it informs but never fires a
measured-strength safety killer. The developmental-vs-adult distinction is load-bearing: a gene
essential for embryogenesis (embryonic/preweaning lethal) may be fully dispensable in adult
tissue, so developmental_only is a caveat, not a hold. Only adult/postnatal lethality
(lethal_ko) is treated as an adult-essentiality safety signal, and even then as an inferred-tier
caution.
Bare "lethality" with no developmental stage is conservatively classed developmental_only (not an
adult killer). A mutant-selective therapy against an activating driver spares the WT copy, further
nullifying an adult-essentiality concern (resolver mechanism-conditioning downgrade).
IMPC-direct fields (impc_*) are VERDICT-INERT corroboration from IMPC release-24.0 via the shared
classifier. IMPC is a PREWEANING-viability + organ-system instrument: its lethal call is
developmental (never lethal_ko), and coverage is PARTIAL (~9k genes) so impc_ko_phenotype_class is
no_phenotype for un-phenotyped genes (KRAS/BRAF/VHL). The primary ko_phenotype_class + its warning
stay on OT-packaged MGI; impc_* corroborate/refine, never drive the verdict.

mutation-drug-response.question: Are cell lines carrying an alteration in {target.symbol} more SENSITIVE to a drug that targets {target.symbol} (PRISM Log2AUC) across the DepMap panel? (Genotype→drug-response biomarker hypothesis.)

warning_predicates.message: Fewer than 3 on-target PRISM compounds; the best-responder Log2AUC vector rests on a thin drug set. Interpret drug_response_stratification_class cautiously.
Mutant-vs-WT Log2AUC difference is statistically significant but sub-threshold in effect (delta > -0.08); at panel n small deltas reach significance — not classified as stratified.

caveats: PHARMACOLOGICAL, not genetic: this measures sensitivity to a DRUG that targets the gene (PRISM Log2AUC), distinct from the CRISPR-KO dependency biomarker (mutation-stratified-dependency). A KO removes noncatalytic scaffolding a small molecule leaves intact, so the two can disagree — they are complementary, not interchangeable.

On-target compound = PRISM CompoundList GeneSymbolOfTargets includes the target (gene-level annotation; a compound with off-target polypharmacology is still counted if it lists the gene). Per-line phenotype is the best-responder (min) Log2AUC across those compounds — the deep-responder tail, not the mean.

Two directional passes: a FORWARD one-sided MW (mutant more sensitive, lower Log2AUC) drives the mutant_*_drug_sensitive classes; a SECOND-PASS reverse MW (mutant more resistant) makes mutant_drug_resistant reachable, gated on its own q + a strong positive delta. Verdict-inert either direction (v1).

Cell-line drug response is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for a clinical predictive biomarker — cell-panel PRISM does not recapitulate patient PK/PD, tumor microenvironment, or resistance evolution (EGFR is the cautionary live example: mutation-stratified in patients, not in the PRISM cell panel).

VERDICT-DRIVING on the GENOMIC gate: the STRONG class (mutant_strongly_drug_sensitive) fires drug_response_biomarker (genomic_alteration.resolver.yaml priority 36), a distinct verdict never conflated with the CRISPR biomarker_stratified_dependency; the MODERATE class is signal-only. The DEPENDENCY spine stays byte-stable (only the genomic gate consumes this card).

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} is elevated on the surface in the {driver}-mutant subset of {indication} (delta_log2={delta_log2}, q={q_value}) — a candidate biologics handle enriched in the {driver}-mutant patient population. Confirm mutant-subset antigen density before nomination.

{target.symbol} / {driver} / {indication} is outside the built mutation-stratified surface slice (v1 = KRAS x NSCLC). COVERAGE GAP — not a determination that the antigen is un-stratified. The gene-level tumor-vs-normal window still applies.

caveats:
A patient-selection-aware SURFACE presence facet: is an antigen elevated in a driver's MUTANT
subset (a biologics handle on the mutant patient population), NOT whether the driver mutation
is itself druggable. Meaningful only for a biologics (antibody/ADC/TCE) lens. ADDITIVE +
verdict-inert: the surface-modality verdict resolves off adc-tce-modality-fit.fit_class; this
contributes a supportive presence signal, not the verdict.
v1 covers ONE archetype: KRAS x NSCLC (LUAD+LUSC). A target/driver/indication outside that
slice reads not_in_product — an honest coverage gap, NEVER a negative. The pan-driver /
pan-indication generalization is a documented follow-on (the derive is parameterized).

HPA `Protein tissue distribution` is pathologist-scored IHC BREADTH (in how many

protein-surface-evidence (surface accessibility) and the RNA normal-tissue signal.

caveats:
QUANTITATIVE normal-tissue PROTEIN comparator (TPHP DIA MaxLFQ mass-spec, 70 adult tissues +
4 fetal germ-layer groups, 663 normal samples; Xu et al., Nature 2026, open PRIDE PXD063370,
CC-BY-4.0). Complements the GTEx/recount3 normal-RNA breadth + the HPA-IHC categorical protein
breadth (normal-tissue-liability) at quantitative PROTEIN resolution — the layer where an
RNA-restricted target can still be broadly protein-expressed.
DIA MaxLFQ abundance is a panel-relative log2 intensity, NOT absolute copies-per-cell; compare
distribution + breadth CLASS and per-tissue relative levels, never treat max_median_log2_abundance
as a concentration. Absolute surface density lives in surface-abundance-density (copies/cell).
The abundance read-out spans ORGANS ONLY (60 solid adult + 4 fetal groups); the 10 non-organ parts
stay in per_tissue_abundance and in the breadth counts, but never name the organ at risk.
Detected-only rows: a (gene, tissue) with n_detected==0 is NOT stored, so a gene absent from the
product reads data_unavailable (coverage gap), and small tissue groups (n_samples 1-2 for rare
organs) should be gated via max_detection_rate / per_tissue_abundance detection_rate before
trusting a single-tissue call.
MEASURABILITY IS LABELLED, NOT GATED. No organ is dropped for thin sampling: on a SAFETY facet a
support gate is fail-OPEN, because a missing organ reads as the favourable "no liability" class.
Read tphp_vital_organ_liability_class against n_vital_organs_unmeasurable — a clean sweep across
measurable organs is not a clean sweep. Dropping n_samples<3 would have deleted blood (n=1) and
thyroid gland (n=2), the organ whose omission was the original S1-3 false negative.

featureless over 20..45 (no valley; only 1.11% of genes in [30,35]), so no threshold is data-nominated.
MKI67 sits at 36, one above the cut: any cut >=37 releases the framework's own proliferation decoy.

blood_compartment entries are one compartment counted four times (v2 tissue_category). The
solid-only counts are emitted for visibility but the CLASSES still use the all-adult count, because
shrinking a denominator under an unchanged ABSOLUTE cut relaxes a safety veto — measured, solid-only
>=35 would fire on 1,446 genes vs 1,510 today, i.e. 64 liabilities silently dropped.
Fetal granularity is the 4 germ-layer groups (ectoderm/endoderm/mesoderm/umbilical cord) the
deposited SDRF exposes, NOT the paper's 22 fetal tissue types; adult subtype resolution is
likewise the organism-part grain. breadth is keyed on ADULT tissues (fetal is developmental
context surfaced via fetal_vs_adult_flag, not the safety-relevant adult footprint).
MIXED ROLE: most fields are additive DISPLAY, but tphp_normal_protein_liability_class is VERDICT-BEARING.
Its broad_and_abundant class fires tvn-tphp-broad-abundant-normal-protein-veto; the skills-side clamp

a KILL — as the sc-normal critical-organ arm). No resolver rung, so the rule is `display` and this card
stays out of card_resolver_consumption. ADC neutral; SM/degrader/BiTE-TCE oppose.

paralog-buffering.question: Does {target.symbol} have functional paralogs that buffer its dependency, and does single-agent inhibition risk paralog-mediated escape?

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} has a strongly-buffering ohnolog paralog ({strongest_paralog_symbol}, delta={strongest_paralog_delta}). Single-agent inhibition risks paralog-mediated escape. Consider dual-target strategies OR degrader modalities that can hit both paralogs.

{target.symbol} shows strong paralog buffering ({strongest_paralog_symbol}, delta={strongest_paralog_delta}), but ohnolog status is UNVERIFIED (raw-CSV fallback). Paralog-mediated escape risk is possible — treat the ohnolog flag as unknown, not absent; re-run against the derived product.

{target.symbol} has annotated paralogs but was not screened in the DepMap 26Q1 dual-KO paralog screen. The gene is a plausible paralog-buffering candidate but the empirical evidence is missing — flag for future screen coverage.

{target.symbol} has NO annotated paralog partner in the DepMap 26Q1 dual-KO screen. AMBIGUOUS — evidence for NEITHER reading: genuinely paralog-free (a real negative) OR absent from the PARIS library. The substrate is a screen, not a paralog annotation. Resolve with an Ensembl Compara lookup.

caveats:
Paralog buffering is a SYNTHETIC-LETHAL signal — the target and its
paralog are individually dispensable but essential in combination. This
is DEPENDENCY HARDENING (single-agent inhibition may fail) — a REQUIREMENT
signal distinct from mutation cooccurrence (co-mutation-and-mutual-
exclusivity card).
v1 covers the DepMap 26Q1 dual-KO paralog screen (PARIS library design):
~7,627 gene-pairs, ~4,475 genes with at least one screened partner. The
Sanger Paralog Screen 2023 is NOT in v1 (no-resale clause; legal review
pending) — v2 will add it plus cross-screen concordance. Genes absent from
the dual-KO library return paralog_buffering_class='data_unavailable'.
`data_unavailable` is AMBIGUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION, never a negative. It merges
(a) gene absent from the PARIS library, (b) partners screened with no
single-KO baseline, (c) product AND raw-CSV fallback unreadable, and (d) a
genuinely paralog-free gene. Only (d) is a real negative, and the one case
this substrate cannot identify: a dual-KO SCREEN is not a paralog
annotation, so a paralog-free gene is absent from the library.
n_paralogs_annotated > 0 isolates (b); at 0 the rest are inseparable.
Consequence of the line above, stated plainly: `none` (annotated, measured,
no buffering) earns small_molecule:supportive via
no-paralog-buffering-sm-supportive, while the STRONGER form of that same
conclusion — no paralogs at all — earns nothing. Honest given the substrate,
not a scoring bug. Closing it needs a genome-wide Ensembl Compara paralog
join at READ time; the product build's join covers ohnolog ancestry of
already-screened PAIRS only, so it cannot supply gene-level absence.
Ohnolog flag (whole-genome-duplication ancestry) is stricter than the
general 'paralog' annotation — ohnologs share cell-type-specific
regulatory context that non-ohnolog paralogs may not. Consumers may
filter to strongest_paralog_ohnolog=true for the highest-confidence
buffering candidates.
Buffering strength cutoffs (strong: delta > 0.5, partial: 0.2-0.5) are
calibrated against published SL screens (SMARCA4/2, ARID1A/B, MAGOH/
MAGOHB). Lineage-conditional cutoffs may be needed in future.
A paralog-buffered dependency does NOT invalidate the target — it
signals that MODALITY CHOICE matters. Degrader modalities (PROTAC,
molecular glue) can hit multiple paralogs if they share ligand-binding
domains; small-molecule active-site inhibitors typically cannot.
Downstream tractability-small-molecule / surface-modality-fit skills should
read paralog_buffering when reasoning about degrader vs SM tradeoffs.

partner-conditional-dependency.question: Is dependency on {target.symbol} stratified by a PARTNER gene's deficiency status across the DepMap panel? (Synthetic-lethality biomarker hypothesis.)

figures.description: Per-cell-line Chronos strip split into Partner-Deficient / Neutral. Reference lines at Chronos = -1.0 + 0. Annotated with the q-value + delta + partner name.

warning_predicates.message: Fewer than 10 partner-deficient cell lines; the synthetic-lethality estimate has wide CI. Interpret partner_stratification_class cautiously.

Deficient-vs-neutral difference is statistically significant but sub-threshold in effect size (delta > -0.2) — at panel n, small deltas reach significance; not classified as partner-conditional (significance != actionable effect). The PARP1×BRCA1 honest-negative shape (delta -0.06, p 0.008).

caveats: Partner-deficiency = the partner is MSI-high (canonical OmicsInferredMolecularSubtypes.csv boolean) OR carries a damaging LoF mutation. The rescue-firing threshold is MODERATE (delta <= -0.2), NOT strong: context-conditional SL effect sizes in mono-KO CRISPR are structurally smaller than own-oncogene addiction (WRN×MSI, a celebrated real SL, is a -0.41 effect). A strong-only threshold would rescue nothing real.

Two directional passes: a FORWARD one-sided MW (deficient more dependent) drives the partner_conditional_*_dependent classes; a SECOND-PASS reverse MW makes partner_neutral_strongly_dependent reachable (verdict-inert). A partner is NEVER credited with a dependency it lacks (forward classes cannot fire on a reverse pattern).

HONEST NEGATIVE by design: a clinically-known SL that is invisible in mono-KO CRISPR (PARP1×HRD — PARPi works by TRAPPING, not loss-of-function; PARP2 buffers) correctly reads not_partner_stratified. The card reports the measurable pooled-CRISPR signal, NOT the clinical mechanism; absence here is not evidence the target is a bad SL.

Curated partner map only — SynLethDB is the candidate-generation source, not a blind auto-join (SynLethDB does not name the alteration type the stratifier requires). A target with no curated partner returns no_partner_mapped (abstains), never a false negative.
Cell-line partner-conditional dependency is necessary but NOT sufficient for a clinical biomarker — needs orthogonal validation (isogenic partner-KO rescue, PDX, patient partner-status).

pathway-activity-context.question: Which PROGENy cancer-signaling pathways are relatively active in the {indication.label} cohort, and is {target.symbol} a responsive gene of any of them?
caveats: Cohort-level RELATIVE pathway-activity landscape, NOT a per-target or per-patient activity call. A target in a cohort where its pathway is relatively_high is not thereby dependent on that pathway — this is a mechanism-context prior, not a dependency or efficacy claim.

PROGENy activity (decoupler MLM) is interpretable RELATIVE to other cohorts (cross-indication z), NOT as an absolute per-cohort on/off — the raw sign depends on the MLM normalization. relatively_high/low key on z>=+1 / z<=-1. Validated cross-cohort: Androgen top in PRAD, Estrogen in BRCA, Hypoxia in KIRC.

Activity is inferred from a downstream transcriptional FOOTPRINT (responsive genes), NOT pathway-member expression — this is PROGENy's design (member expression is a poor activity proxy). Top-100 responsive genes/pathway.

VERDICT-INERT: drives no resolver rung. Sibling of phospho-pathway-activity / signaling-network-mechanism in the Mechanism space; upgrades that gate from topology-only to quantitative activity as advisory context.

pathway-node-leverage.question: Given the biology, is {target.symbol} the best NODE to hit within its complex / pathway neighbourhood, or is it dominated by a more-dependent / more-tractable member?

warning_predicates.message: Node-leverage computed pan-cancer (no indication, or the lineage cohort too thin). Pan-cancer Chronos makes context-specific drivers look dominated (BRAF, CTNNB1) and hides context-specific SL (SMARCA4->SMARCA2). Treat a 'dominated' call as low-confidence until a lineage-scoped read is available.

No complex or pathway node-set contains the target. A peripheral regulator that no tight (CORUM / GO:BP) set contains is itself a differentiation signal — but the leverage call cannot be made from the lenses implemented here (complex + GO:BP).

caveats: SOFT, verdict-inert context: contributes no hard-gate veto and never raises certainty. It is DepMap-Chronos-derived (correlated with the dependency cards) and feeds the differentiation axis only.

Common-essential exclusion is always applied (DepMap CRISPRInferredCommonEssentials); without it, housekeeping genes (VCP, AARS1) crown themselves as the dominant node of any pathway. The target itself is RETAINED even if common-essential — that is its own safety signal, not a leverage disqualifier.

Lineage-scoped in production; pan-cancer is an explicit, flagged fallback (evidence_scope). Pan-cancer Chronos makes context-specific drivers look dominated and hides context-specific SL — interpret pan-lineage verdicts cautiously.

Node-set is a LENS on a precision/recall gradient: complex (CORUM, tightest/mechanistic) is more trustworthy than pathway (GO:BP, high-recall/noisy). Report each lens with its precision caveat; do not average across lenses.

Tractability-yield uses Pharos TDL only (Tclin > Tchem > Tbio > Tdark) — a coarse druggability proxy, not a target-specific chemical-matter assessment. dominated_but_tractability_edge means 'a stronger node exists but is no more druggable than the target', not 'the target is druggable in absolute terms'.

Undirected membership (co-complex / co-annotation) CANNOT ground an 'acts-through' direction claim — no directed SIGNOR/OmniPath check is performed. The verdict is a leverage comparison, not a mechanistic epistasis claim.

Paralog/combinatorial correction (spec §6): single_ko_leverage_understated flags a paralog-buffered target (strong/partial, from the DepMap dual-KO product) whose single-KO leverage UNDERSTATES its dependency — a buffered weak/dominated call is a candidate false-negative; assess dual-KO leverage. Target-level FLAG (additive, verdict-inert; does not re-rank); paralog product optional/fail-soft.
A minimum median-Chronos separation gate (min_median_separation) prevents dominant/dominated being called on screen noise; nodes within the gate are treated as indistinguishable.
