pathway-stratified-surface.question: Is the surface antigen {target.symbol} elevated in the {signature}-HIGH subset of {indication} tumors vs {signature}-LOW — a biologics handle on that tumor compartment?

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} is elevated on the surface in the {signature}-HIGH subset of {indication} (delta_log2={delta_log2}, q={q_value}) — a candidate biologics handle enriched in that tumor compartment. Confirm subset antigen density before nomination.

{target.symbol} / {signature} / {indication} is outside the built pathway-stratified surface slice (v1 = HALLMARK_HYPOXIA x NSCLC). COVERAGE GAP — not a determination that the antigen is un-stratified. The gene-level window still applies.

caveats:
A tumor-STATE-conditioned SURFACE presence facet: is an antigen elevated in a pathway/stress-HIGH
subset (a biologics handle on that compartment), NOT whether the pathway is itself druggable.
Meaningful only for a biologics (antibody/ADC/TCE) lens. ADDITIVE + verdict-inert: the
surface-modality verdict resolves off adc-tce-modality-fit.fit_class; this contributes a
supportive presence signal, not the verdict.
HONEST CONFOUND: in v1 (HYPOXIA x NSCLC) the top hits are squamous-signature-dominated (DSG3/DSC3/
PKP1, GJB3/5/6) — hypoxia correlates with squamous histology (LUSC), so the pathway-HIGH tertile is
LUSC-enriched. Read pathway_high_up_surface as "the hypoxic/SQUAMOUS niche", not pure hypoxia; a
histology-adjusted split is the refinement. CA9 (girentuximab hypoxia-ADC antigen) still validates
as pathway_high_up_surface — an out-of-set positive control.
v1 covers ONE archetype: HALLMARK_HYPOXIA x NSCLC (LUAD+LUSC). A target/signature/indication outside
that slice reads not_in_product — a coverage gap, NEVER a negative. Pan-signature generalization is a
documented follow-on (the derive is parameterized by --signature/--indication).
Statistics: per-sample signature score = mean log2-TPM over the HALLMARK members; tertile split
(top vs bottom third, middle excluded); Mann-Whitney U (high vs low) + BH-FDR across surface genes.
pathway_high_up_surface requires q<=0.10 AND delta_log2>=0.5. underpowered (a tertile arm < 10) is
INADMISSIBLE, not a negative. An expression difference is not an antigen-density guarantee — confirm
surface protein density + homogeneity in the pathway-high subset before an ADC/TCE nomination.

phospho-pathway-activity.question: Is {target.symbol} phosphorylated (pathway-activity proxy) in {indication.label} tumors, and beyond its total abundance — or is no phosphorylation detected?
caveats: phospho_not_detected is a MEASURED no-detection, NOT a claim the target is unphosphorylatable. The phospho panel covers ~4.7-6.1k genes/cohort vs ~7.4-11.5k for total protein, so ~48-55% of protein-detected genes have zero phosphosites, and ~1.7-2.3k of those per cohort DO carry sites in another CPTAC cohort. Read phosphoprotein_detected_in_other_cohorts before inferring biology: true means this cohort's zero is a DETECTION gap (e.g. KRAS 0 in coad but 2 in ccrcc; MET 0 in brca, 8 in ccrcc).

When the target's total protein is not detected in the same cohort, the class is data_unavailable with phospho_axis_uninformative_reason=total_protein_not_detected_in_cohort — phosphopeptide absence is unreadable when the protein itself is undetected (e.g. ALK in LUAD, a fusion-activated RTK below bulk-MS detection). Never read that as evidence against phosphorylation.

phospho_exceeds_abundance compares mean phospho z-score to mean total-protein z-score across tumors; a target can be abundantly phosphorylated simply because it is abundant (phospho_present) vs hyper-phosphorylated beyond abundance (phospho_active). Interpret with the abundance cards (Q1/Q5).

Detection fraction reflects MS coverage (a phosphosite below the MS detection limit reads as absent); low detection is not proof of no phosphorylation. Phosphosite-level stoichiometry is not resolved.

The phospho signal is total across the target's sites (mean); a SPECIFIC activating site (e.g. an autophosphorylation site) is not singled out — top_phosphosites lists the most-detected sites for follow-up but does not assert which is functionally activating.
CPTAC bcm phospho is the harmonized cptac-package source; it is a tumor cohort (no matched-normal contrast in this card — that is a follow-up).

pmhc-epitope-evidence-iedb.question: Does {target.symbol} have experimentally-validated epitopes in IEDB — peptides observed presented on human HLA and/or recognized by T cells (which class / how many alleles, in a cancer context)?
caveats: IEDB experimentally-annotated epitopes: the CANCER / self-antigen minority filtered to HUMAN source protein + human MHC (HLA allele or blank). Presentation / immunogenicity GROUND TRUTH complementing hla-ligand-atlas-presentation-per-protein-v1 (benign normal-tissue immunopeptidome breadth); the two are distinct pMHC lenses.

Presentation / recognition != expression, and != PREDICTED binding: this is experimental epitope evidence (what has been observed in positive assays), distinct from mRNA / protein abundance and from in-silico HLA-binding prediction.

ASSAY ASYMMETRY: a positive assay is strong evidence; ABSENCE (not_observed / no_positive_epitopes) is WEAK — a peptide below assay coverage may still be a real epitope. Never read absence as a confirmed non-epitope. This card is IEDB tumor-context-agnostic: a cancer-context flag, not a tumor-restriction call.

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} peptides are presented on >= 19 normal tissues (HLA {hla_class}). A TCR-mimetic pMHC TCE would engage every presenting cell — a broad on-target/off-tumor liability. A peptide-centric program needs a tumor-restricted peptide + tight HLA restriction, not just presentation.

{target.symbol} is absent from the HLA Ligand Atlas benign immunopeptidome. MS tracks abundance x turnover, so absence is a WEAK negative — a tumor-restricted peptide-centric CANDIDATE to confirm on a tumor atlas, NOT proof it is unpresented.

caveats:

NORMAL tissue" (the safety denominator) — NOT "is it tumor-presented". The tumor-restriction call
needs a tumor immunopeptidome (PCI-DB PXD058376 + indication PXDs — a Tier-2 acquisition). A
restricted_presentation call is necessary-but-not-sufficient for a clean pMHC-TCE target.

turnover. PRESENCE is strong evidence; ABSENCE (not_observed) is WEAK — a peptide below MS detection
on normal tissue may still be presented. Never read not_observed as a confirmed non-presenter.

restricted to specific HLA alleles; the peptide-level allele + 1000G super-population coverage is a

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} was not resolvable in STRING v12 or CORUM. Interactome is UNKNOWN, not empty — a coverage/resolution gap, never 'has no interactions'.

{target.symbol} is a STRING hub (>=50 high-confidence interactors). High connectivity can indicate a promiscuous/central protein — interpret 'interactor' lists as functional-association context, not direct binary binding partners (STRING combines many evidence channels).

caveats:
Two signals reported SEPARATELY, never merged: STRING functional-association degree (how connected)
vs CORUM stable-complex membership (part of a named machine). STRING edges are multi-channel
functional associations (co-expression, text-mining, databases, experiments), NOT necessarily
direct physical binding; the high-confidence cutoff (combined_score >= 700) is STRING's canonical
threshold. CORUM complexes are curated stable assemblies.
Target-intrinsic (cancer-independent): the same regardless of indication. This card takes no
indication and emits no verdict — descriptive molecular context for the target-intrinsic dossier.
THIRD signal (method 1.1.0): BioGRID experimental-PHYSICAL interactions
(physical_interactome_class + n_physical_interactors + top_physical_partners), from
biogrid-physical-interactions-per-gene-v1 (BioGRID 5.0.259). Unlike STRING's functional score,
these are experimentally-OBSERVED physical bindings, ranked by distinct supporting-publication
count (evidence depth + traceability, e.g. TP53-MDM2 in 504 papers). Alongside STRING/CORUM, never merged.
Symbol resolution: STRING is self-contained (9606.protein.info maps symbol<->ENSP); CORUM
(UniProt-AC-keyed) resolves symbol->AC via a target_id_resolver sidecar. Pinned to STRING v12 +
CORUM 5.3. License: STRING CC-BY-4.0; CORUM CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial).

precog-prognostic-association.question: Across 166 datasets (~18k patients), does {target.symbol} expression track overall survival in {indication.label} (pan-cancer meta-analytic prognostic prior)?
caveats: HYPOTHESIS-GENERATING, NOT a clinical claim. PRECOG meta-Z aggregates UNIVARIATE (unadjusted for stage/grade/age) per-dataset Cox associations across 166 heterogeneous datasets (varied platforms, cohorts, normalization). A robust meta-Z is a strong prognostic PRIOR, but not a multivariable-validated biomarker.

META-ANALYTIC CORROBORATION of expression-clinical-association (Q11), NOT a replacement. Q11 is a single TCGA cohort (indication-specific, patient-level, but often underpowered); PRECOG is pan-cancer + far better powered but per-cancer-type columns are noisier than the pooled pan-cancer meta-Z. Read them together: agreement raises confidence; divergence flags a cohort-specific vs pan-cancer effect.

PROGNOSTIC (expression<->survival), NOT clinical-PRECEDENT (drugs-in-clinic). This does NOT fill the license-walled `clinical` risk_category (Cortellis/IQVIA); it is a biomarker-axis prognostic facet routed to differentiation/prognostic context.

expression_high_better_survival is NOT a target killer — it flags that the prognostic/targeting rationale differs (the target may mark indolent disease); interpret alongside dependency + genomic evidence.

INDICATION CROSSWALK: PRECOG's 39 cancer-type columns are idiosyncratic. When precog_indication_approx is True the indication is a documented approximation (COADREAD→Colon_cancer: no rectal split; NSCLC→Lung_cancer_ADENO: representative histology). LUAD/LUSC/SCLC map exactly. Unmapped indications return data_unavailable (pan-cancer meta-Z still surfaced as context).
VERDICT-INERT: drives no resolver rung. A pan-cancer meta-analytic prognostic prior surfaced to render/LLM alongside the single-cohort survival card.

prism-compound-activity.question: For compounds annotated as targeting {target.symbol}, how many exist across PRISM screens, what is their dose-response potency (Log2AUC) across cell lines, AND is that activity lineage-selective or pan-cancer? Is the target druggable in the clinical library (small-molecule tractable), tool-compound-only (druggable but pre-clinical), or first-in-class opportunity (no annotated compound)?

figures.description: Horizontal bar of the top-K compounds by activity (bar length = −median Log2AUC; Repurposing compounds fall back to −single_dose_lfc, tagged (LFC)). Bars colored by clinical status (navy = OncRef-prioritized clinical; ochre = tool / Repurposing). Annotations: drug_name (y-axis) + MOA + polyselective

Per-lineage median Log2AUC horizontal bar (top 10 lineages most-active-first). Navy bars = lineage active (median Log2AUC < -0.15); gray = inactive/borderline. Each bar labeled with the top compound + n_lines + best-responder LFC (surfacing median-vs-tail divergence). Dashed reference at the active

Text card showing class + granular fields (n_compounds, highest_phase, median Log2AUC, best-responder LFC, polyselective-count) AND lineage-selectivity + n_lineages_active/evaluated. Complements the bars for headline-only surfaces; renders informatively even when the bars are placeholders.

warning_predicates.message: All compounds annotated to this target are polyselective (targeting >1 gene). Activity signal may be caused by off-target engagement; discount before interpreting as 'target-relevant kill'.
Multiple tool compounds exist but no clinical anchor. Target may be druggable but preclinical; SM programs would be first-in-clinic risk profile.

Compounds annotate to this target but no OncRef Log2AUC measurement exists (annotation may be Repurposing-only). Class call rests on annotation presence + single-dose LFC; dose-response potency is unmeasured.

Pan-cancer median Log2AUC is flat but per-lineage aggregation is lineage-selective. Pan-cancer signal is diluted by non-responding lineages; consult per_lineage_activity for the biomarker-cohort read (expected shape for oncogene-addiction drugs like KRAS-G12C inhibitors).

Lineage medians flat despite ≥3 annotated compounds. Check per_lineage_activity.best_responder_lfc — a strongly-negative best-responder with flat median indicates a genotype-specific responder subpopulation (canonical for KRAS-G12C-type drugs). Mutation-conditional stratification is a future target.

caveats:
PRIMARY metric is Log2AUC (dose-response-curve integral, DepMap-portal
default). This replaces v1/v2's single-dose median-LFC. Log2AUC ranges
(-∞, 0]; non-responders sit near 0, active drugs push negative (typical
clinical hits -0.3 to -1.0). Interpret median_log2auc as pan-cancer POTENCY,
not per-line kill magnitude.
best_responder_lfc is a SEPARATE raw-LFC tail statistic (min across all
compound × dose × cell_line entries). It preserves deep-responder magnitude
(LFC -3 to -5) that Log2AUC's 0-cap compresses. When median Log2AUC is flat
but best_responder_lfc is deeply negative, the target has a genotype-specific
responder subpopulation — the oncogene-addiction signature.
Repurposing 24Q2 has NO AUC file (single-dose screen). Its compounds are
ANNOTATION-ONLY in v3: they appear in top_compounds + n_compounds_targeting
(metric_source='single_dose_lfc') but do NOT contribute to median_log2auc,
per_lineage_activity, or lineage_selectivity — those are OncRef-Log2AUC-only.
A gene annotated ONLY in Repurposing has median_log2auc=null +
lineage_selectivity=data_unavailable even with n_compounds_targeting > 0.
highest_clinical_phase is APPROXIMATED. The PRISM source files do NOT carry a
clinical-phase column. `phase_1_plus` is inferred from OncologyReference 25Q4's
`Prioritized=TRUE` flag; `preclinical` from non-prioritized OncRef; `tool` from
Repurposing-only presence. A future upgrade would join to ChEMBL's `max_phase`.
PRISM's "compound targets gene X" annotation does NOT guarantee that the
compound's activity is caused BY target engagement — LONAFARNIB "targets KRAS"
via farnesyltransferase inhibition, not direct binding. Interpret activity as
"response in cell lines annotated to this target" NOT "on-target killing."
`no_compounds_found` is a REAL class, not a data-gap — a first-in-class
opportunity, NOT a killer. Distinct from `data_unavailable` (parquet unreadable).
Lineage-selectivity uses THRESHOLD-BASED classification on Log2AUC (≥1 lineage
median < -0.15 active, ≥1 median > -0.05 inactive) — NOT a formal enrichment
test as in E2. Coarser signal, scipy-free precompute. Per-lineage n varies
widely (5 to ~110 lines); interpret rank confidence proportional to n_lines_screened.

prism-crispr-concordance.question: For compounds annotated as targeting {target.symbol}, does their per-cell-line kill pattern correlate with CRISPR-KO Chronos AND RNAi-KD dependency across the DepMap cell-line panel? Which specific cell lines are dual-validated as both CRISPR-dependent AND compound-responsive?

figures.description: 2D scatter: rho(PRISM, CRISPR-Chronos) on x-axis, rho(PRISM, RNAi-DEMETER2) on y-axis, one point per annotated compound. Quadrant coloring: upper-right (both ≥ 0.30) = triangulated navy; right-only = CRISPR-confirmed light-blue; upper-only = RNAi-confirmed light-green; other = gray. Dashed reference

Horizontal paired bars: for each dual-responder cell line, |Chronos-dep| (red) alongside |best-compound-LFC| (navy). Sorted by CRISPR-dep magnitude descending. Right-annotated with the driving compound ID. Answers 'which specific cell models are dual-validated?' — natural biomarker cohort for the ta
Text card: class label + best rho vs CRISPR + best rho vs RNAi + n_dual_responders + top-3 dual-responder cell lines with their Chronos + LFC values.

warning_predicates.message: Neither CRISPR Chronos nor RNAi DEMETER2 data available for this gene. Cannot validate compound target engagement via genetic-chemical concordance. Coverage gap; not a discordance signal.

PRISM compound activity does NOT correlate with CRISPR-KO or RNAi-KD dependency. Annotated compounds may work via off-target mechanisms. Target itself may still be valid; a different chemical scaffold could engage. Compound-annotation warning, NOT target killer.

Triangulated concordance is strong (both CRISPR + RNAi track with compound activity) but NO individual cell line clears both dual-responder thresholds. Response may be graded rather than distinct responders; consult per_compound_concordance.

CRISPR-confirmed but not RNAi-corroborated engagement may indicate paralog compensation revealed only by full KO. Consider whether degrader-modality (full depletion) engages the same biology; RNAi KD-residual suggests remaining protein activity is sufficient.

caveats:
Correlation is Spearman rank (robust to outliers) computed across cell
lines that appear in BOTH the CRISPR/RNAi panel AND the compound's PRISM
screen. Minimum 20 lines required. Genes/compounds with sparser overlap
return thin_evidence.
RNAi (DEMETER2) uses shRNA — partial KD, not full KO. Genes that require
complete inhibition (e.g. some kinases, degrader-only targets) may show
CRISPR-only concordance because the RNAi-KD residual is sufficient to
rescue viability. This is the crispr_confirmed_engagement class; not a
signal that the compound is off-target.
Correlation direction: positive rho = target-engaged. Both Chronos and
LFC are NEGATIVE for dependent/killed cells; two negatives correlate
positively when concordant.
discordant_off_target_likely is a compound-annotation warning, NOT a
target killer. If PRISM's annotated compounds don't validate target
engagement, the target may still be biologically valid — a different
chemical scaffold could engage it. Interpret alongside E1 (dependency)
and E5 (predictability) for the target-itself signal.
dual_responders are cell lines meeting both hard thresholds (Chronos <
-0.5 AND best-compound-LFC < -1.0). Triangulated targets with graded
responses across the panel may have strong rho but few individual
dual-responder lines. The correlation (per_compound_concordance) is the
primary signal; dual_responders is the discrete-cohort follow-up.
RNAi panel is smaller (~700 lines) than CRISPR (~1500 lines), and the
CCLE→ModelID bridge drops ~11 lines whose CCLEName lookup fails. When
n_intersected_rnai << n_intersected_crispr for the same compound, RNAi
concordance carries more variance; interpret rnai_confirmed_engagement
with caution when n < 30.

protein-domains-class.question: What is {target.symbol}'s curated domain architecture, and what molecular protein class(es) does it belong to?

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} has no curated UniProt domain AND no class-bearing keyword (or is not resolvable to a UniProt AC). Architecture/class is UNKNOWN — a curation/coverage gap, never 'featureless'.

{target.symbol} has a protein-class keyword but NO curated FT DOMAIN (e.g. a transcription factor whose DNA-binding is annotated as a 'region', not a 'domain'). The protein_class is informative; domain_architecture is legitimately empty, not missing.

caveats:
Two axes reported together (they share the UniProt substrate): DOMAIN architecture (FT DOMAIN, the
modular structure) + PROTEIN CLASS (mapped from UniProt keywords, the functional type). A protein
legitimately has MULTIPLE classes (an adhesion-GPCR is both gpcr AND cell_adhesion) — protein_class
is a LIST; protein_class_primary is a convenience (first keyword-order class), not authoritative.

class keyword / unresolvable). protein_features_class stays curated-only for vocabulary stability.

~15,019 proteins (6,445 have an InterPro domain but NO curated FT DOMAIN — e.g. KRAS 'Small
GTP-binding domain', TP53 'DNA-binding domain', whose regulatory regions UniProt annotates as
'region' not 'domain'). type=domain hits from interpro-109-0-snapshot-2026-08-05. Read
domain_evidence (curated | both | interpro_only | none) to know the architecture's provenance.

resistance-emergence-signature.question: When {target.symbol} is inhibited by its anchor drug, which gene knockouts rescue the cell (candidate resistance mediators)?

warning_predicates.message: The anchor drug for {target.symbol} was screened in <=1 model — resistance calls rest on a single context; treat as hypothesis-generating.
No drug-anchor CRISPR screen for {target.symbol} (the panel covers KRAS/KIT/XPO1 only). This is a coverage gap — absence of a resistance signal here is NOT evidence against resistance mechanisms.

caveats: Signal = gene-effect(drug arm) - gene-effect(control arm) (Chronos-difference). POSITIVE = the rescuer's KO becomes LESS essential when the target is inhibited (the drug's effect depends on that gene; losing it blunts the drug) = a candidate resistance mediator.
Self-target rows (rescuer == inhibited target — KO of the drug's own target) are a self-consistency artifact and are dropped upstream; they never appear as mediators.

DepMap drug-anchor screens cover only single-target anchor INHIBITORS (KRAS via MRTX1133, KIT via Avapritinib, XPO1 via Eltanexor). Absence of an anchor screen is a coverage gap (no_anchor_screen), never evidence against resistance (measured-vs-null).

A significant rescuer is a resistance HYPOTHESIS to monitor (loss-of-function, deletion, or downregulation of the gene as a resistance route), not a proven clinical resistance mechanism — read the biology (KRAS/MRTX1133 -> NF1 RAS-GAP reactivation, KEAP1/NRF2 antioxidant program, NF2/Hippo bypass are all validated; not every hit will be).

This is a GENETIC rescue signal in cell lines; it does not by itself establish clinical resistance or its frequency. Transcriptional (Tahoe-derived) and clinical resistance layers are orthogonal follow-ons.

caveats: TUMOR-grain sibling of cellline-rna-protein-concordance (cell-line). Same measurement_type, different grain (target_indication vs target). Report the two SIDE-BY-SIDE, never averaged — their disagreement (e.g. KRAS partial in cell lines, poor in COAD tumors) is the decision-relevant signal.
CPTAC cohort maps to the indication (COADREAD→coad, KIRC→ccrcc, LUSC→lscc, PAAD→pdac, etc.); indications without a CPTAC cohort return data_unavailable.
bcm protein abundance is NOT zero-centered (per the matched product manifest) — used for CORRELATION only (scale-invariant), never cross-gene comparison.
A poor_proxy verdict is a MODALITY caution (protein must be measured for ADC/TCE; RNA biomarker inadequate in THIS tumor type), NOT a target killer.
Bulk-tumor concordance is degraded by purity/stroma; a low r may partly reflect microenvironmental dilution rather than pure post-transcriptional decoupling (see Q9 purity attribution).

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} shows scRNA expression in safety-essential normal cell types: {safety_essential_flags}. Check modality tolerance — essential-cell-type expression is a primary BiTE/TCE safety concern.
{target.symbol} is detected at >20% cells in {n_cell_types_above_20pct} distinct normal cell types — broad normal-tissue RNA footprint across cell lineages.

{target.symbol} scRNA normal-tissue assessment unavailable (no tissue shard for indication, or insufficient donor coverage). Normal-cell-type liability is UNKNOWN, not low — do not read absence as a favorable window.

caveats:
scRNA Census pseudobulk (mean log1p CP10K + detection fraction per donor×cell_type) reflects
TRANSCRIPT, not protein. Low-abundance surface targets (GPCRs, CD antigens with regulated
expression) are systematically under-detected by scRNA. Complement with HPA IHC (protein) and
membrane proteomics where available.
Cell types are raw CELLxGENE Census Cell Ontology labels. Naming consistency varies across
contributing atlases (e.g. 'colonocyte' vs 'colon epithelial cell'). Detection-fraction
aggregation is done within canonical labels; cross-label synonyms are not merged at this tier.
n_cells >= 10 filter applied at Tier-1 aggregation: donor-cell-type groups with fewer than 10
cells are excluded (statistically unreliable detection estimates). Small cell populations in
sparse tissues may be systematically absent.
Coverage grows as additional tissue shards land (sc-normal-celltype-expression-{tissue}-v1).
For indications without a matched tissue product, the result is data_unavailable — this is
a coverage gap, not a confirmed safety pass.
MIN_RELIABLE_DONORS = 5: if a cell type is represented by fewer than 5 donors with n_cells >= 10,
that cell type is not used for classification. Very rare normal cell types (e.g. enteroendocrine
cells in colon from small atlases) may be under-represented.

sc-surface-normal-safety-solid.question: Is {target.symbol}'s SURFACE protein displayed on normal SOLID-tissue safety-essential cell types (kidney/heart/spleen/thymus/lymph-node) at single-cell CITE-seq resolution — the biologics-deciding on-target/off-tumor floor beyond the immune compartment?

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} SURFACE protein on a NON-origin critical solid organ cell type ({max_surface_tissue}: {max_surface_cell_type}, mean-CLR {max_mean_clr}) — a bulk-invisible on-target/off-tumor hazard for a TCE/ADC/mAb. Safety caution, arbitrated by modality + therapeutic window.

{target.symbol} surface protein is displayed on {n_celltypes_surface_displaying} distinct normal solid-organ cell types (mean-CLR >= 1.0) — broad normal-tissue SURFACE footprint. Narrow the therapeutic window before an unmasked biologic.

{target.symbol} solid-tissue normal SURFACE assessment unavailable (target absent from the CITE-seq surface panel, or insufficient donor coverage). The solid-organ surface floor is UNKNOWN, not low — do NOT read absence as a favorable window.

caveats: PROTEIN, single-cell, SOLID-organ sibling of sc-surface-normal-safety (immune/PBMC) and the SURFACE analogue of sc-normal-celltype-expression (RNA) + normal-tissue-liability (bulk HPA-IHC total protein). Report all four SIDE-BY-SIDE — surface protein decouples from both RNA and total protein; this is the solid-organ surface-specific off-tumor floor.

Class keys on PEAK cross-donor mean-CLR, NOT positive fraction: ADT ambient/spillover makes a per-cell CLR>0 count fire on ~every lineage (over-call); the mean-CLR level separates true surface display from spillover. Same discipline as the immune sibling.

high_surface_on_normal_solid / critical_organ_surface_liability is a SAFETY CAUTION (biologics on-target/off-tumor risk), NOT a target killer — its severity is arbitrated by modality + therapeutic window (modality-therapeutic-window) and the safety resolver. not_surface_detected_normal_solid is FAVORABLE.

origin_tissue_surface_liability (surface display confined to the tumor's tissue-of-origin) is therapeutic-window-arbitrated, NOT a hard veto — a validated on-tissue ADC target must survive it. Only NON-origin critical-organ surface display fires the hard caution.

A target ABSENT from the solid-tissue CITE-seq surface panel returns data_unavailable — not surface-profiled on solid organs, NEVER a safety pass. Coverage grows as additional HuBMAP / Tabula Sapiens-surface organ shards land.

CITE-seq surface panels are ANTIBODY-PANEL-LIMITED: a target is only assessable if an ADT probe was in the panel. Panel absence is a coverage gap (data_unavailable), distinct from measured non-display. min_reliable_donors=5 per tissue x cell type.

sc-surface-normal-safety.question: Is {target.symbol}'s SURFACE protein displayed on normal immune cell types (single-cell CITE-seq) — an on-target/off-tumor hazard for a biologic — and how broadly?
caveats: PROTEIN, single-cell sibling of sc-normal-celltype-expression (RNA) + normal-tissue-liability (bulk IHC). Report SIDE-BY-SIDE — surface protein decouples from both RNA and total protein; this is the surface-specific off-tumor floor.

Class keys on PEAK cross-cell-type mean-CLR, NOT positive fraction: ADT ambient/spillover makes a per-cell CLR>0 count fire on ~every lineage (over-call); the mean-CLR level separates true display (CD8A ~4.4 on T) from spillover (~ -1 on B).

high_surface_on_normal_immune is a SAFETY caution (broad/high normal-immune surface display = on-target/off-tumor risk for a TCE/ADC), NOT a target killer; not_surface_detected_normal_immune is FAVORABLE (e.g. BCMA reads not-detected on normal immune).

v1 = peripheral immune (Hao 2021 PBMC) + bone marrow (NeurIPS 2021 BMMC), unioned; class = PEAK across all cell types (either compartment is an off-tumor floor). Solid-tissue (HuBMAP) safety-essential organs are the follow-on shard. A target ABSENT from every panel returns data_unavailable — not surface-profiled, never a safety pass.

caveats: SINGLE-CELL SURFACE-grain sibling of cellline-rna-protein-concordance + rna-protein-concordance-tumor. Same measurement_type, new grain (single-cell surface). Report SIDE-BY-SIDE, never averaged — the point is that surface protein decouples from RNA MORE than total protein does.

Metric is PEARSON across cell types (RNA detection fraction vs mean CLR ADT); Spearman is retained but diverges for lineage-restricted markers (a marker on ONE cell type scores ~0 under Spearman yet is a perfect proxy — Pearson rewards the aligned spike). Classified on Pearson at 0.6/0.3.
A poor_proxy verdict is a MODALITY caution (the scRNA surface-presence argument is inadequate; protein must be confirmed for an ADC/TCE/mAb), NOT a target killer.

v1 scope is the IMMUNE compartment (Hao 2021 PBMC; sample_context normal). Tumor-cell surface concordance requires tumor CITE-seq. A target ABSENT from the panel returns data_unavailable — not surface-profiled by ADT, an honest coverage gap, never a pass.

shed-ectodomain-liability.question: Is the extracellular domain of {target.symbol} proteolytically shed as a soluble circulating decoy, creating an antigen-sink liability for antibody / ADC / T-cell-engager modalities?

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} has a clinically-established shed ectodomain ({shed_product}; serum marker {serum_marker}). A soluble decoy sequesters antibody/ADC/TCE drug before tumor delivery. Require a membrane-proximal epitope and model the antigen sink in dosing. Not a small-molecule concern.

{target.symbol} is HPA-annotated as secreted — a proxy that a soluble form may circulate as a partial antigen sink for biologics. Weaker than a clinical serum-marker; confirm with isoform-resolved / soluble-antigen measurement before an antibody/ADC/TCE nomination.

Shedding status of {target.symbol} could not be evidenced (not in the curated shed vocab; no HPA secretome signal). COVERAGE GAP, not a determination that the ectodomain is not shed — structured sources under-annotate shed receptors. Treat shed liability as UNKNOWN for biologics.

{target.symbol} is empirically released into conditioned media across DepMap lines (Olink NPX {media_mean_npx} >= panel-high {media_panel_high_npx}, n={media_n_lines_detected}) — a MEASURED shed signal corroborating an antigen-sink liability for biologics. Opposing, not killer.

caveats:
A shed ectodomain is a liability SPECIFIC to antibody-based modalities
(antibody / ADC / bispecific T-cell-engager). It is IRRELEVANT to an
intracellular small-molecule target. The composed, modality-scoped card
applies this signal only in a biologics lens.
Signal severity is `opposing`, never `killer`. Approved and late-stage
biologics exist against shed antigens (mirvetuximab soravtansine targets
the shed-capable FOLR1; anti-MUC16 and anti-MSLN programs are in advanced
trials). A shed ectodomain de-prioritizes and constrains the design (drives
epitope choice toward the membrane-retained fragment and sink-aware dosing)
— it does not categorically foreclose the modality.
This is DISTINCT from isoform-selectivity (isoform_selective_targets.yaml).
Shedding = the full-length epitope is present on the tumor cell AND targetable,
but a soluble copy circulates as a decoy. Isoform-loss = the dominant tumor
variant lacks the epitope entirely (p95HER2, EGFRvIII). ERBB2 and MET appear
in BOTH vocabularies with different mechanism-of-failure and mitigation; a
governance reader should consult both.
The `clinically_shed` tier is grounded in FDA-cleared / widely-used serum
tumor markers (a serum tumor marker IS a shed ectodomain by clinical-chemistry
definition). This is the RELIABLE tier and the only one that reliably covers
shed receptor tyrosine kinases (HER2-ECD, sMET), which structured shedding
databases (MEROPS, TopFIND) systematically miss. The HPA/UniProt PROXY tier
is broader but noisier and biased toward signal-peptide-route secretion.
`indeterminate` (could-not-evidence) is deliberately NOT collapsed into
`not_shed`. There is no clean, redistributable, structured, oncology-complete
shedding system-of-record (per a deep-research survey: SheddomeDB has no
bulk download, TopFIND is CC-BY-ND, MEROPS is frozen and misses shed RTKs).
Absence of a shedding annotation therefore carries high false-negative risk
and must not be read as a trusted negative.
MEASURED facet (measured_shed_class, v1.1.0): Olink NPX in DepMap CONDITIONED MEDIA is
the empirical shed readout — protein a live cancer cell released into supernatant. A
PARALLEL categorical: it corroborates or adds measured nuance to shed_liability_class
but NEVER alters it (a clinically_shed antigen stays clinically_shed even if it reads
media_shed_low). Only media_shed_high is verdict-relevant (opposing); low /
not_on_secreted_panel are informational.
MEASURED facet — three load-bearing limits: (i) PANEL BOUND — the Olink media panel is
~1,038 proteins, secretome-preselected, so `not_on_secreted_panel` is NON-informative
(never a measured "not shed"); (ii) IN-VITRO — cell-line supernatant shedding models,
does not prove, an in-vivo circulating-antigen sink (MSLN/FOLR1 read low in vitro);
(iii) some shed RTKs (CEACAM5, ERBB2) are off the panel entirely — the curated clinical
tier remains the reliable cover for those.
Future upgrades: (a) add MEROPS sheddase→substrate cleavage evidence (ADAM10/17,
BACE1) as a mechanistic tier if LGPL redistribution is legally cleared; (b) a
genome-wide UniProt CHAIN/PEPTIDE-vs-topology shed classifier to broaden the proxy
tier beyond the HPA secretome column; (c) extend the curated vocab as new shed
antigens are characterized.

shet-lof-intolerance.question: What is {target.symbol}'s continuous dominant-LoF selection coefficient (s_het, GeneBayes), and does it corroborate or sharpen the binary gnomAD constraint call for on-target safety?
caveats: VERDICT-INERT (Phase 1): fires no interpretation rule and drives no safety resolver rung, so the safety verdict is byte-stable. It is a continuous CORROBORATION of the binary gnomad-lof-constraint call (agreement/disagreement). A verdict-bearing s_het rung is a deferred, backtest-gated follow-up.

s_het (GeneBayes, Zeng et al. 2024) is a DOMINANT-LoF selection coefficient — intolerance to HETEROZYGOUS LoF. It is continuous and better-calibrated than binary pLI/LOEUF, catching dosage-sensitive small genes constraint misses. Higher = more intolerant. Read shet_score alongside the 95% CI (shet_lower_95/upper_95).

A HIGH s_het is an on-target safety concern for a FULL-KO modality (degrader / RNA / full-inhibition SM); it is DOWNGRADED for a mutant-selective (alteration-role GoF) mechanism — that conditioning lives in the per-modality safety layer, not this card. CC-BY-4.0: cite Zeng et al. 2024 Nature.

caveats:
PROVENANCE / COMPOSITION. methods.call=signor-mechanism-network names SIGNOR as the primary
curated source, but the live dispatch composes the network via the mechanism_composed method:
a UNION of curated edges — SIGNOR (Jul2026 source release; curator-tight, causally-directed,
~30k human interactions) + CollecTRI ONLY — whose edges set network_class. Reactome is layered
as pathway CONTEXT (reactome_pathway_context), NOT counted in the network_class edge total.

identify what modality could act at that mechanism, NOT what modality
will succeed against this target. The tractability-small-molecule and
surface-modality-fit skills perform the joint reasoning across
MoA-relevance + structural features + surface-topology to reach
modality-fit conclusions.

product (primary pushdown); the composed MoA/context layer is composed on-read from the signor-jul2026
SOURCE release. A source re-pull surfaces as a new dated SIGNOR release, giving consumers an explicit

SELECTIVITY WINDOW (window_verdict): the AND-gate is a CONTRAST — tumor same-cell co-positivity (high) vs normal same-cell co-positivity (~0). window_open = tumor coordinated AND no well-powered normal cell type co-expresses both; no_window = a normal cell type DOES (the SAFETY negative bulk + tumor-only avidity both miss).

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} has a clinically-dominant alt isoform ({isoform_selective_dominant_isoform}). Modality letter grades suppressed. See vocabularies/isoform_selective_targets.yaml v{vocabulary_version_isoform}.

Raw endocytosis motif count is high but high-confidence count (pLDDT-accessibility-filtered) is low. Many predicted motifs likely fall in unstructured cytoplasmic-tail regions and may not mediate internalization. ADC-favorability arguments should use endocytosis_motif_count_high_confidence.

Multi-pass TM protein with limited extracellular residue area. ADC / TCE epitope-accessibility is likely compromised — even if the target is 'on the surface', antibody engagement may be sterically constrained.

caveats:
TMbed benchmarks at ~89% TMH-count accuracy per Bernhofer & Rost 2022.
Multi-TM SLC transporter families are the weakest class. Consumers with
modality stakes should verify against UniProt TOPO_DOM annotations for
critical targets — the surface-topology-and-ptm card is a first-pass
filter, not engineering-grade coordinate.
ECD orientation is heuristic: for type-I/II single-pass this is the
biologic extracellular domain; for multi-pass it is the longest
extracellular loop; for GPI-anchored proteins the heuristic may miss
the anchor context. Consumers should cross-reference UniProt topology
annotations for critical modality decisions.
Endocytosis motif detection is regex-based (YXXΦ, NPXY, Dileucine).
YXXΦ is a 4-residue motif that occurs by chance ~once per 400 residues
in random protein sequence; a 200-residue cytoplasmic tail will have
~0.5 false hits. The reviewer-driven pLDDT-accessibility filter
(`endocytosis_motif_count_high_confidence`) cross-references AlphaFold
predictions to filter false positives — downstream rubric weights
consume ONLY the high-confidence count.

dominant alt isoform in the isoform_selective_targets vocabulary v1.

(vIII), BRAF (fusions), MDM2 (splice variants), CD19 (Δex2), FGFR2
(IIIb/IIIc/fusions). See vocabularies/isoform_selective_targets.yaml
for citations + regulatory context. Curation is opt-in; genes without
entries are treated as gene-level-safe by default.

synthetic-lethal-partners.question: Does {target.symbol} have a curated synthetic-lethal partner (SynLethDB v3), and is the evidence experimental — such that a pooled non-dependent CRISPR read may be a context-conditional false negative?

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} has an experimentally-supported synthetic-lethal partner ({sl_partner_count} total). A pooled non-dependent CRISPR read is NOT a trusted negative — may be a context-conditional dependency. Suppresses the dependency veto to insufficient; does NOT nominate.
{target.symbol} has curated SL partner(s) but computational-prediction only — weaker evidence. Surfaced for context; does NOT suppress a dependency veto (the gate requires an experimental partner).

caveats:
ANNOTATION, not measurement. A curated SL relationship suppresses a dependency VETO
to `insufficient` (the pooled negative is not trusted); it NEVER nominates a target
(annotation ≠ a measured dependency) and NEVER suppresses pan_essential (a common-
essential target is not rescued by an SL partner). Symmetric to how the biomarker-
stratified-dependency suppressor works (nomination_verdict_gate.yaml).
Evidence tier is load-bearing. `has_experimental_partner` (CRISPR/RNAi/throughput
screen) is the trustworthy suppressor. A computational-only prediction is surfaced
(`has_computational_sl_partner`) but does NOT suppress a veto — SynLethDB's
computational tier is deep-learning-predicted and false-positive-prone.
COMPLEMENTS paralog-buffering, does not replace it. Paralog-buffering is the DUA-
measured, intra-gene-family self-rescue signal (MARK2↔MARK3 dual-KO delta);
SynLethDB is the published/citable layer catching ARBITRARY partner-conditional SL
(SMARCA2←SMARCA4) that intra-family measurement cannot see. Both feed Gate-C
veto-suppression through their respective mechanisms.
`no_curated_sl_partner` is a REAL read (the gene is in the SL universe, no partner
found), distinct from `data_unavailable` (the derived product was unreachable) —
measured-vs-null discipline: absence of a curated partner is not a coverage gap.
SynLethDB v3 (CC-BY-4.0) aggregates published SL screens across species; this card
consumes the HUMAN, Tier-1 (experimentally-supported + computationally-predicted)
table only. Tier-2 (deep-learning top-1% predictions) is excluded — it would flood
the index with low-confidence partners.

tahoe-drug-perturbation.question: Which small molecules significantly move {target.symbol}'s expression (suppress or induce), and in how many cancer lines (single-cell drug-perturbation MoA)?
caveats: VERDICT-INERT mechanism/MoA facet. A transcriptional drug-response is TARGET-ENGAGEMENT (was the gene/pathway moved), NOT dependency (does the cell need it) and NOT selectivity. Backtest (Pilot 2): Tahoe drug-response did NOT concord with DepMap CRISPR essentiality — engagement != dependency. Read alongside the functional-requirement dependency verdict, never as a substitute.

not_measured is a coverage/measurement gap (no significant DE row at padj<0.25 — may be an ncRNA/pseudogene absent from the resolved set, or a gene genuinely unmoved by the screened drugs), NOT a mechanism claim. Distinct from data_unavailable (read failure).

MoA recovery is pathway-dependent (Pilot 2: strong for proteasome/MEK inhibitors, but BRAF inhibitors PARADOXICALLY reactivate ERK in RAS-WT lines so a BRAF drug may not suppress ERK-output; mTOR readouts are soft). A drug appearing as a strong mover of a gene is an MoA hypothesis, not proof of a specific mechanism.
All cell-line (Tahoe = 50 cancer cell lines); patient-tumor transfer is untested. Median across lines/doses hides context-specificity; n_cancer_lines indicates breadth.

The gene's OWN transcript response is measured — an oncogenic driver (e.g. KRAS) may read weakly_perturbed because its biology is not transcriptional, whereas a pathway-output gene (e.g. DUSP6) moves strongly. Interpret the class relative to the gene's expected regulation.

target-safety-prioritisation.question: How does Open Targets prioritise {target.symbol} on its engineered safety-relevant scores (safety-event, genetic constraint, mouse-KO), as orienting context?
caveats:
All fields are Open Targets ENGINEERED PRIORITISATION SCORES (normalized ~[-1,+1], higher =
more favorable), NOT raw measurements. Do NOT read geneticConstraint as a gnomAD LOEUF or
isInMembrane as a boolean — the dedicated per-fact cards (gnomad-lof-constraint,
surfaceome-family-classification) carry the authoritative values. Orientation, not evidence-of-record.
A `not_in_prioritisation_table` status means the target is absent from OT's 78,691-target
prioritisation set (not a coverage failure of any single fact) — read it as "OT has no engineered
prioritisation profile for this target", not as a negative safety signal.
OT's prioritisation sign convention is subtle and version-specific; this card is intentionally
verdict-inert so a sign-convention misread cannot flip a safety call. The dedicated per-fact
cards carry the actual measured human-genetics safety signals.

tcga-til-fraction-saltz.question: By H&E deep-learning (Saltz 2018), what is the absolute tumor-infiltrating-lymphocyte fraction in {indication}, and does it corroborate the CIBERSORT CD8 hot/cold call?
caveats: VERDICT-INERT display corroborator (like cellline-protein-abundance-procan): fires no rule, moves no verdict. An ABSOLUTE H&E deep-learning TIL fraction that orthogonally corroborates the immune-context relative CIBERSORT CD8 hot/cold call (same TCGA participants, different modality). Agreement HARDENS confidence; it does not create or override the CD8 call.

COVERAGE: 13 TCGA studies ONLY (BLCA BRCA CESC COAD LUAD LUSC PAAD PRAD READ SKCM STAD UCEC UVM); any other indication → data_unavailable (fail-closed, never imputed). Absolute-threshold bins on the per-indication median til_percentage are COARSE — read median_til_percentage + n_samples, not the class alone.

til_percentage = fraction of H&E image patches classified TIL-positive by a deep-learning model (Saltz et al. 2018); morphology-based, antibody-independent. Join key is the 12-char TCGA ParticipantBarcode. CC-BY-3.0/TCIA — cite Saltz et al. 2018 + TCIA DOI 10.7937/K9/TCIA.2018.Y75F9W1.

temporal-setting-expression-shift.question: Does {target.symbol} expression shift between primary and metastatic (or treatment-naive vs post-treatment/relapsed) {indication.label} tumours — i.e. is the target still expressed in the disease setting where the drug would be used?
caveats: Setting strata (primary vs metastatic; treatment-naive vs post-treatment/relapsed) come from annotated/paired cohorts (MSK-MET, GENIE-BPC, paired primary-metastatic RNA); these are NOT randomized — a shift may reflect cohort composition (biopsy site, prior-therapy selection), not intrinsic target biology.

BLOCKED (blocked_needs_per_sample_reader): no per-sample setting-annotated RNA reader has landed; the per-setting record panorama is deferred until a per-sample substrate exists. This card emits cross-setting reducer scalars only.

A stable or gained call in the advanced/post-treatment setting is the reassuring translational read (target still present where the drug is used); a lost call is a patient-selection / trial-setting caveat, NOT a veto (measured-vs-null: absence of setting data is not evidence of stability).
Metastatic-site RNA carries a stromal / microenvironment confound distinct from the primary site; cross-setting deltas implicitly condition on biopsy site.

tumor-elevation-breadth.question: Across how many cancer indications is {target.symbol} elevated in tumor vs normal — at the protein layer (CPTAC) and/or the RNA layer (pan-cancer DESeq2) — as pan-cancer tumor-presence breadth?

figures.description: Pan-cancer by-tissue expression: a log2(TPM+1) boxplot per TCGA study (tumor) and per GTEx tissue (normal), co-plotted on ONE recount3/GENCODE-v26 axis, each block sorted by median. The per-tissue tumor-vs-normal distributions underlying the K-of-N breadth roll-up.

warning_predicates.message: {target.symbol} is protein-elevated in only ONE CPTAC cohort — a single-cancer signal, not pan-cancer breadth. Treat as indication-specific; do not generalize the tumor-presence claim across cancers.
{target.symbol} was not quantified in any CPTAC cohort — pan-cancer tumor-elevation breadth is UNKNOWN (coverage gap; CPTAC covers 10 cohorts), NOT low. Do not read absence as 'not elevated'.
{target.symbol} was quantified in fewer than 3 CPTAC cohorts — the breadth denominator is small, so the breadth class is weakly powered. Interpret K-of-N cautiously.

{target.symbol}'s protein breadth (CPTAC) and RNA breadth (pan-cancer DESeq2) DISAGREE — one layer elevated across cancers, the other a measured not_tumor_elevated. Do NOT average; inspect both. Usual cause: post-transcriptional regulation or protein under-detection.

caveats:
Breadth is over INDICATIONS for ONE target ("in how many cancers"), NOT a ranking
over targets and NOT selectivity within a single cancer. For "is it up in THIS
tumor" use tumor-protein-abundance-cptac (the per-indication tumor-vs-normal contrast);
for "how many cancers at all" use this card.
"Elevated" = the per-cohort protein_expression_class is strong_up or modest_up,
which already encode q<0.05 significance gating in the underlying CPTAC DEG. This
card COUNTS those calls — it introduces no new statistics and inherits the
underlying MSstatsTMT limma-eBayes moderated-t provenance.
CPTAC covers 10 cohorts (BRCA, CCRCC, COAD, GBM, HNSCC, LSCC, LUAD, OV, PDAC,
UCEC). n_cohorts_tested is the target's coverage WITHIN those, not all cancers. A
low breadth count on a target tested in few cohorts is under-powered, not
necessarily narrow — see the narrow_cptac_coverage warning.
data_unavailable (target absent from all CPTAC cohorts) is a COVERAGE GAP, never a
measured negative. not_tumor_elevated (tested, elevated in none) IS a measured
negative. The vocabulary keeps the two distinct — do not conflate.
Protein-level breadth does NOT imply surface accessibility. An intracellular
protein elevated across many tumors is not thereby biologics-actionable — pair with
protein-surface-evidence + surface-topology cards for modality decisions.
TWO breadth layers, surfaced ALONGSIDE (never averaged): PROTEIN
(tumor_elevation_breadth_class; CPTAC, 10 cohorts) is primary; RNA
(rna_tumor_elevation_breadth_class; pan-cancer DESeq2, 27 indications) is a parallel
view over a larger indication set. A target can be protein_only (post-transcriptional
or RNA gap) or rna_only (protein gap — CPTAC's 10 vs RNA's 27).
breadth_layer_concordance names the relationship; read both, do not collapse to one.
RNA breadth "elevated" is VINTAGE-STABLE: it keys off dominant_direction +
cells_supporting + magnitude (cells A/C of the sensitivity design, identical across
all 27 products' cell-B vintages), NEVER off cell B — whose meaning differs by
vintage (ComBat-TSS / design-comparison / skipped-in-UCEC). See the
pancan-dge-tumor-vs-normal-v1 manifest's cell_b_semantics column.

warning_predicates.message: Normal arm has < 10 samples in this CPTAC cohort — protein tumor-vs-normal calls are underpowered. Interpret protein_expression_class cautiously.

Protein is strongly upregulated but RNA (tumor-rna-vs-adjacent card) is not significant. Post-transcriptional regulation elevates protein beyond RNA — this pattern is ADC/TCE-favorable but should be verified with additional evidence.

caveats:
CPTAC-PDC declared md5 + size are advisory (stale) per source manifest;
the compute layer trusts streamed md5. See methods/cptac_protein_deg/
for the ingest discipline.
Protein abundance is TMT-labeled mass-spec ratio-based. Absolute
intensity is NOT copies-per-cell — the surface-abundance-density card
(Phase F) derives copies-per-cell separately using HPA IHC intensity
anchoring. Slaga 2018 (Sci Transl Med) established the TCE viability
threshold at > 1,000 copies/cell.
10 CPTAC cohorts do NOT cover all TCGA indications. Missing: BLCA,
SKCM, KIRC, STAD, ESCA, LIHC, CESC, PRAD, CHOL, ACC. For those
indications, tumor-rna-vs-adjacent (RNA) remains the primary
presence signal.
Small normal arms (GBM, OV, PDAC): stat_test_used='skipped_low_n' when
< 5 samples per arm. Consumers should treat those rows as data-
unavailable for statistical claims.
Protein-level presence does NOT guarantee surface accessibility — a
protein highly expressed in tumors that is exclusively intracellular
is not ADC/TCE-actionable. Cross-reference the surface-topology-and-ptm
+ surfaceome-family-classification cards before treating a strong_up
call as modality-actionable.

tumor-protein-distribution-by-subtype.question: How does {target.symbol} tumor protein abundance (CPTAC TMT) DISTRIBUTE across the molecular subtypes of {indication.label} — which strata are enriched or depleted vs the pooled cohort?
caveats: DESCRIPTIVE / verdict-inert: subtype is confidence/context for patient selection, NOT a new veto — the pooled tumor-protein-abundance-cptac card carries the protein read; this card enriches it.

COADREAD-only (2026-08-21): cptac-subgroup-assignments-coadread-v1 (MSI_H/MSS from MMR-IHC) is the only landed CPTAC assignment shard. MSI is an MMR-IHC surrogate; ~43% of aliquots are is_member=null (not tested). Other indications return subtype_axis_available:false until their shards land.

CPTAC whole-cell-lysate TMT measures PRODUCED protein (tumor-vs-reference log2 ratio), NOT surface-accessible antigen; small per-stratum n means MSI_H is frequently underpowered (see subtype_axis_quality).

Cross-arm comparability (2026-09-18): `enriched` is NOT the same claim across the three by-subtype arms. This arm cuts at a 0.25 log2 tumor-vs-reference RATIO shift; tumor RNA cuts at 0.585 and cell-line RNA at 1.0, both on log2(TPM+1) medians. The cuts differ in VALUE and in UNITS, so they are not commensurable. Each row now emits the applied subtype_enrich_log2_delta, so a cross-layer read can normalise or decline to join the arms instead of silently equating them.

A stratum in the 10-29 exploratory band (subgroup_exploratory_floor) emits its distribution stats with evidence_state: exploratory and never a scoped call. This is a SECOND, lower visibility band, not a relaxation of subgroup_n_floor, which keeps its one meaning (>=30) on every substrate.

tumor-rna-distribution-by-subtype.question: How does {target.symbol} RNA expression DISTRIBUTE across the molecular subtypes of {indication.label} tumors — which subtypes are enriched, depleted, or restricted vs the pooled distribution?
caveats: Consumed tumor assignment shards, verified 2026-09-18 (11, every one now declared in required_inputs): 6 base TCGA (COADREAD, HNSC, STAD, NSCLC serving LUAD+LUSC, ESCA, PAAD) + 4 orthogonal TCGA MAF driver-strata shards (HNSC, NSCLC, ESCA, PAAD) unioned onto the base strata + the NON-TCGA sclc-subgroup-assignments-v1 (George 2015 NAPY). An indication outside applies_when returns subtype_axis_available:false (honest) until its shard lands.

normal_comparator_type distinguishes matched (true GTEx tissue-of-origin) from proxy (histological analogue, e.g. HNSC→esophagus/skin/salivary — GTEx has no head-and-neck track). A PROXY window is WEAKER evidence: proxy fields live in proxy_normal_windows, NEVER in the matched fraction_tumor_above_normal_* fields. The panel is multi-proxy because a target's window can be strong vs one proxy but weak vs another (EGFR/HNSC: ~86% vs esophagus/salivary but ~33% vs skin).

A stratum below subgroup_n_floor (n<30) carries distribution stats for context but a NULL subtype_signal — never a scoped call on underpowered data. The reader HAS now opted into the exploratory band (AM #662), so a 10-29-member stratum grades `exploratory` rather than being invisible: still a null signal, still excluded from every cross-stratum reducer, but labelled hypothesis-grade instead of discarded.

The UUID→barcode→stratum bridge drops the ~8% of recount3 samples with no sidecar barcode or no stratum label; a <5% match rate raises the id-convention guard rather than masquerading as empty strata.
MSI-H / CIMP-High stratum biology is dominated by mismatch-repair hypermutation; subtype-specific calls may partly reflect global expression dysregulation, not target-specific signal.
Subtype is confidence/context for patient selection, NOT a new veto — the pooled tumor-rna-distribution card carries the presence verdict; this card enriches it.

tumor-rna-distribution.question: How does {target.symbol} RNA expression DISTRIBUTE across {indication.label} tumors — median, fraction of patients detectable/high, and shape (continuous, bimodal, long-tail)?

figures.description: Per-sample tumor (TCGA) vs matched-normal (GTEx) log2(TPM+1) distribution (box + strip), with the normal-p95 line and the fraction-of-tumors-above-p95 annotation. Shows the distribution SHAPE + the target-high subset the median hides.

warning_predicates.message: Fewer than 30 tumor samples for this indication — distribution shape (bimodality, tail) is weakly powered. Interpret distribution_pattern cautiously.
No matched GTEx normal for this indication — the fraction-above-normal-p95 overlay is unavailable; distribution stats are tumor-only.

caveats: Per-sample log2(TPM+1) from recount3/GENCODE-v26 (same pipeline as GTEx normal → directly comparable).
distribution_pattern uses a dependency-light gap heuristic (not a KDE/dip test), robust on small panels; a `bimodal` call is a patient-selection hypothesis, not a statistical guarantee.
RNA distribution does not imply protein; pair with the CPTAC protein cards for ADC/TCE decisions.

tumor_expression_class == subset_high is a PATIENT-SELECTION hypothesis, not a population claim: it can fire on as few as 10% of patients (high_fraction >= 0.1 AND a bimodal/long_tail shape), so acting on it needs a prevalence read and a selection biomarker. It now carries its OWN presence rung (tumor-expression-subset-high-supportive -> tumor_subset_high_expression, below tumor_broadly_expressed), so a 10%-high and a 60%-high target no longer collapse to one verdict — read high_fraction too.

subset_high is EMPIRICALLY UNREACHED here, and the binding conjunct is the SHAPE, not the 0.1 floor: measured 2026-09-19 over the 41-package eval corpus (generated, not tracked), distribution_pattern was continuous on 36/36 tumor-card instances and subset_high fired 0x, while the SAME heuristic returned bimodal/long_tail on 11/37 cell-line instances. Within ONE TCGA indication, >=20% of tumors below TPM 1 AND >=20% above TPM 50 rarely co-occur, so absence of subset_high is weak evidence.

The fraction_tumor_above_normal_p95 fields are a matched-normal OVERLAY for context; the tumor-vs-normal selectivity VERDICT lives on tumor-vs-normal-selectivity (Gate B), kept separate from this presence/distribution card.

The splicing_* fields are from TCGA SpliceSeq per-event PSI (patient tumours), a SEPARATE substrate from the recount3 expression above; they measure alternative-splicing dysregulation, not expression level, and never move tumor_expression_class.

splicing_dysregulation_class is a bulk-cohort POPULATION view: a low-frequency/context-specific cancer isoform (e.g. AR-V7 in castration-resistant disease, largely absent from treatment-naive TCGA) reads 'stable' because it does not move cohort PSI variance. This is orthogonal to the curated isoform_selective_targets guardrail, by design; absence of a shift is not absence of a clinically-relevant isoform.

n_tumor_shifted_events is null when the indication has no matched normals (9/33 TCGA cohorts); in that case only the variability signal (highly_variable/stable) is available, not the tumour-vs-normal shift.

{target.symbol} has no TPHP tumor-vs-normal protein value for this cohort (target absent, or the indication has no TPHP carcinoma cohort) — protein corroboration UNKNOWN (coverage gap), not flat. The CPTAC card (tumor-protein-abundance-cptac) + the RNA selectivity cards remain authoritative.

caveats:
VERDICT-INERT corroboration facet. TPHP DIA-MS tumor-vs-normal protein, complementing the
CPTAC TMT-MS card (tumor-protein-abundance-cptac) across 22 carcinoma cohorts, several outside CPTAC
coverage. Fires no rule / no veto; consumed via the derived rna_protein_tvn_concordance read, and is
absent from card_resolver_consumption.
NOT AN INDEPENDENT PLATFORM from normal-tissue-protein-abundance-tphp. The normal arm is the TPHP
body atlas of the tumour's own organism part — the same samples that card summarises (a cohort's
n_normal_samples_total equals that part's atlas n_samples on all 22 cohorts), NOT a separately
collected adjacent normal. One DIA-MS measurement read twice. A consumer counting corroborating
protein platforms must collapse the two on normal_arm_source or it manufactures confirmation.
UNPAIRED and UNPAIRABLE: a Welch two-sample t-test on group medians, BH within cohort. There is no
patient to pair to — the normal arm is an atlas, not the same donors. A DIFFERENT estimator from
the CPTAC MSstatsTMT limma-moderated t, so a cross-card disagreement can reflect assay/estimator
(DIA MaxLFQ vs TMT; unpaired-Welch vs moderated-t), not only biology.
DETECTION CENSORING, DECLARED NOT CORRECTED: arm medians are over DETECTED samples only, so
missing-not-at-random dropout biases protein_effect_size toward tumor-DOWN (3.60:1 down:up over
q<0.05 rows; 1.50:1 where both arms are complete). log2_fc is deliberately NOT re-centred. Gate any
directional read on protein_detection_complete; false means CONFOUNDED, not absent. Rows are never
dropped for it (58.1% of genes have no complete row in any cohort).
Effect magnitudes rest on small normal arms (n_normal 3-74); treat as a corroborating facet, not a
standalone DEG call, and gate on n_normal_samples against n_normal_samples_total. DIA MaxLFQ
abundance is a panel-relative log2 intensity, NOT absolute copies-per-cell (surface-abundance-density
owns copies/cell).
22 of 29 TPHP carcinoma cohorts are retained (7 dropped for insufficient matched-normal). Whole-cohort
BRCA / head&neck (HNSC) / ovarian are NOT resolvable here (breast is subtype-split; HNSC is ambiguous
across tongue+larynx; ovarian was dropped) → data_unavailable, and the CPTAC + RNA cards remain
authoritative for those.

warning_predicates.message: Comparator-dependent: significant cells disagree on direction. Typically tumor up vs GTEx-population but flat/down vs TCGA-adjacent-margin (field effect), or vice versa. 'Which normal?' changes the call — inspect the 3-cell forest before trusting either direction.

Only TCGA-adjacent cells (A/B) ran — no GTEx tissue maps to this indication. cells_supporting is capped at 2/2; selectivity vs population-normal is UNTESTED. Treat a '2/2' as weaker evidence than a full 3/3.

Only the GTEx cell (C) ran — TCGA adjacent-normal below the DESeq2 sample floor for this indication. cells_supporting is capped at 1/1; the within-patient field-effect contrast is UNTESTED and there is no cross-comparator robustness.

caveats:
cells_supporting AS A FRACTION of cells_ran (≤3) is the trust anchor, NOT any
single log2FC. The cells bracket two irreducible uncertainties: WHICH normal
(TCGA-adjacent vs GTEx-population) and HOW to handle batch (raw vs ComBat). A
gene at 3/3 is differential no matter how you frame the comparison; a gene at
1/3 is an artifact of one specific framing. Do not cite a log2FC without its
cells_supporting / cells_ran.
Cell D (tumor vs GTEx, ComBat(source)) was RETIRED, not run. Source (TCGA/GTEx)
is perfectly confounded with group (tumor/normal) in the joint contrast, so
ComBat-seq regressed out the genuine tumor signal along with the source effect —
the intended "pessimistic floor" read as noise, not signal (confirmed on the
full COADREAD cohort). The pipeline now assembles only cells A/B/C
(06_four_cell_driver.R:227-244); the GTEx comparator survives as the naive cell C.
TCGA paired-adjacent-normal (cells A/B) is a surgical selection artifact —
uninvolved margin chosen at the surgeon's discretion, often bearing
tumor-adjacent transcriptional signatures ("field cancerization"). This is
WHY cells C/D (GTEx) exist as an orthogonal comparator; discordance between
the A/B and C/D pairs is the field-effect signal made explicit.
GTEx normal tissue (cells C/D) is BULK RNA — cell-type-specific expression
within a tissue can far exceed the tissue median (e.g. intestinal crypt
cells vs whole colon). Selectivity at bulk-RNA level does not guarantee
selectivity at cell-type-of-origin level.
Selectivity at RNA level does not guarantee selectivity at protein or
surface level. Pair with protein-surface-evidence card (HPA/CPTAC-based)
when available.
All three cells share ONE alignment substrate (recount3 monorail). This is
deliberate: mixing aligners (e.g. GDC-STAR for adjacent, recount3 for GTEx)
would confound comparator with aligner and defeat the sensitivity logic. As
a consequence, cell A does NOT byte-match the prior-generation GDC-STAR
tumor-vs-adjacent product; it agrees in direction + rank, not in magnitude.

interpretation) and the gene-level alteration-role — a DISTINCT claim, not a CIViC corroborator.

variant-level-interpretation.question: For {target.symbol}, which specific variants are oncogenic (vs VUS/benign), and which confer therapy resistance — the per-variant call the gene-level role and recurrence axes can't make?
caveats: PER-VARIANT interpretation aggregated to the GENE. civic_variant_class is the STRONGEST oncogenicity call among the gene's variants — inspect oncogenic_variants for the specific alleles. Oncogenicity precedence: graded AMP/ASCO/CAP Oncogenic assertion (authoritative) > CIViC Oncogenic evidence-direction > Functional GoF/LoF/Dominant-Negative > Predictive-Sensitivity-implied (a therapy responding to a variant implies an actionable driver; only lifts an unknown/VUS call, never overrides an explicit benign). SIGNOR (SIGnaling Network Open Resource) Jul2026 quarterly release —
the authoritative expert-curated signaling-interaction catalog.

  - RESIDUE + SEQUENCE (modification-site coordinate + 7-residue window)

  - PMID citation
  - Verbatim q

coverage_vocab.captured: framework wires real data for this axis; a correct read is expected.
coverage_vocab.blind: framework does not model the deciding evidence for this axis.

bands.necessity: Is this real, actionable biology? Modality-independent. (was 8-gate A–D + Altered). ANY-OF, NOT conjunctive (M2): a target may satisfy necessity via ANY path — an antigen-driven target (FOLR1/DLL3/MSLN/CLDN18.2) carries NO recurrent somatic alteration, so an UNFIRED `genomic_alteration` must NOT be read as failing necessity. `mechanism` is a characterization member (advisory), not a gate.
bands.sufficiency: Will it become a drug in THIS modality? Per-lens. (was 8-gate E–H)

questions.question: Is the target expressed / present in the tumor?
questions.evidences: RNA transcribed / protein made (recount3 + DepMap + CPTAC).

questions.question: Is the target selective for tumor vs normal (adjacent=efficacy; population=safety)?
questions.evidences: tumor-vs-normal window (recount3 4-cell DESeq2; adjacent + GTEx comparators).

questions.question: Is the target a functional dependency / driver, and in which context?
questions.coverage_note:
partial: pooled pan-cancer scalar conflates six dependency modes (only oncogene-addiction
fully wired). Context-conditional modes are biomarker_facets reporting into this question.

questions.question: What is the target's network position / MoA hook / PD marker?
questions.coverage_note: advisory-only today; does not move the deterministic verdict (characterization, not a gate).
questions.evidences: network position / MoA hook (SIGNOR + CollecTri + Reactome + kinome).

questions.question: How is the target genomically altered (SNV / CN / fusion), and which class drives?
questions.evidences: somatic alteration landscape (TCGA-MC3 + GENIE): mutation / CN / fusion frequency.

questions.question: Is the target druggable by a small molecule (compound exists + agrees with genetics)?
questions.coverage_note: partial: retrospective PRISM + pocket ligandability wired; degrader feasibility + medchem tractability not.

questions.question: Does surface biology support a biologics modality (ADC / TCE / antibody)?
questions.coverage_note:
partial (review H1: CORRECTED from a stale `blind`). surface-abundance-density is LIVE (derives
estimated_copies_per_cell + a 5-level surface_density_class vs the TCE floor; resolver carries
measured below-floor downgrade rungs). REAL blind legs: the DERIVED surface-density MS product
(method built, product not yet materialized) + endocytosis/turnover for ADC-vs-TCE discrimination
+ avidity/co-expression. NOTE: gate_coverage.yaml v2 still baselines this `blind` and the
target-profile deciding-axis router reads that — a coordinated router migration to `partial` is
tracked separately (cross-repo; skills CI asserts the current blind baseline).
questions.evidences: topology + surfaceome-family + LIVE surface-abundance-density (CPTAC + calibrated copies/cell ladder vs the ~1000/cell TCE floor) + shed + therapeutic-window; ADC/TCE fit_class composed.

questions.question: Is the target intolerant of loss-of-function / does normal-tissue liability threaten a therapeutic window?
questions.coverage_note: partial: germline constraint + HPA IHC breadth wired; normal-tissue-SURFACE window (biologics-deciding) thin. Modality-tiered.
questions.evidences: germline LoF constraint (gnomAD) + normal-tissue liability (HPA IHC).

questions.question: Is the target differentiated (co-mutation landscape, precedent, biomarker definability)?
questions.coverage_note: partial -> license_blocked for the decisive axis: clinical precedent + competitive differentiation are commercial-license-walled (Cortellis/IQVIA/Flatiron).
questions.evidences: co-mutation / mutual-exclusivity + biomarker definability (TCGA-MC3 + GENIE Fisher).

questions.question: Can the nomination be preclinically validated (patient-derived models, PD/imaging assays, combination/resistance)?
questions.coverage_note: blind by construction — translational-readiness is a descriptive partial skill; not in the nomination fan-out.
questions.evidences: patient-derived model coverage (HCMI) — one leg wired; PD/imaging/internal-model legs unbuilt.

questions.question: What does the target depend on / combine with RELATIONALLY — synthetic-lethal partners, measured dual-KO co-dependencies, combination co-targets under inhibition, and resistance mediators?
questions.coverage_note:
RELATIONAL: the answer is a RANKED PARTNER LIST (partner × interaction-type × evidence ×
direction), not a scalar verdict — forcing it into a scalar gate is the Archetype-B trap.
Today fragmented across 3 standalone single/two-card skills + 2 edge cards homed in
functional-requirement (paralog-buffering, partner-conditional-dependency). Consolidation
target = the combination-and-vulnerability skill; see relational_consolidation.
questions.evidences: curated SL (SynLethDB v3) + measured dual-KO GI (DepMap ParalogV2 + published) + drug-anchored combination/resistance CRISPR screens (DepMap 26Q1).

questions.question: Does the target's OWN locus feature (copy-number / promoter methylation) explain its OWN expression AND its OWN dependency — a coherent cis-driven addiction, or co-occurring but mechanistically-independent axes?
questions.coverage_note:
GATELESS coherence owner: the answer is a 2×2 leg interaction (does CN/methylation drive the
target's own expression, and does that expression predict its own dependency), NOT a scalar gate.
Owned by the cis-feature-coherence skill; CIS_DOSAGE/SILENCING/EXPR_DEP/CONJOINT claim_vector with
cross-grain TCGA-patient corroboration. Registered as a first-class question 2026-08-21 to close
the #479 dangling primary_axis (cis-feature-coherence pointed here before the axis existed).
questions.evidences: cell-line CNV / methylation × expression × dependency coherence (DepMap 26Q1) + cross-grain TCGA-patient corroboration.

insufficient_underpowered.plain_english: Not enough data to call — honest abstention.

insufficient.plain_english: Not enough data to call — honest abstention.

dependency.label: Dependency
dependency.plain_english: Is the target genetically required in these cells?

selectivity.label: Tumor selectivity
selectivity.plain_english: Is the target more present/dependent in tumor than normal?

genomic_alteration.label: Genomic alteration
genomic_alteration.plain_english: Is the target recurrently mutated / copy-altered / fused?

mechanism.label: Mechanism
mechanism.plain_english: What signaling role and MoA hooks does the target have?

surface_modality.label: Surface modality fit
surface_modality.plain_english: Does surface biology support an ADC/TCE biologic?

tractability_small_molecule.label: Small-molecule tractability
tractability_small_molecule.plain_english: Is there a compound, and does chemistry agree with genetics?

cis_coherence.label: Cis coherence
cis_coherence.plain_english: Do locus -> expression -> dependency line up?

synthetic_lethal_partners.label: Synthetic-lethal partners
synthetic_lethal_partners.plain_english: Which partner losses make the target essential?

target_development_level.label: Target development level
target_development_level.plain_english: What is the target's Pharos/IDG Target Development Level (druggability/novelty tier) + family?

mutation_cooccurrence.label: Mutation cooccurrence
mutation_cooccurrence.plain_english: Which genes co-occur with or are mutually exclusive to target mutations?

antigen_pair_coexpression.label: Antigen pair coexpression
antigen_pair_coexpression.plain_english: Do two surface antigens co-express on the SAME malignant cells (same-cell avidity for an AND-gate bispecific / dual-targeting biologic)?

pdx_drug_response.label: Pdx drug response
pdx_drug_response.plain_english: Does the target's drug-response signal reproduce IN VIVO — do treatments naming the target produce tumour regression in PDX population trials (Novartis PDXE)?

amp_expr_stratified_dependency.label: Amp expr stratified dependency
amp_expr_stratified_dependency.plain_english: Is target dependency stratified by whether the line is both amplified and high-expression for the target (amplification-driven overexpression-addiction)?

mutation_variant_class_spectrum.label: Mutation variant class spectrum
mutation_variant_class_spectrum.plain_english: What variant classes does target carry in cell lines (missense vs LOF vs mixed = oncogene/TSG pattern)?

precog_prognostic_association.label: Precog prognostic association
precog_prognostic_association.plain_english: Across 166 datasets (~18k patients), does target expression track overall survival (pan-cancer meta-analytic prognostic prior)?

antigen_internalization.label: Antigen internalization
antigen_internalization.plain_english: Is target's surface antigen internalized upon antibody binding (endocytosis efficient enough for ADC payload delivery), and what is its surface turnover — the axis routing ADC-viable vs TCE-only?

tumor_vs_normal_protein_abundance.label: Tumor vs normal protein abundance
tumor_vs_normal_protein_abundance.plain_english: Does target's tumor-vs-adjacent-normal PROTEIN differential hold at the protein layer across the TPHP DIA-MS carcinoma cohorts (the RNA->protein corroboration of tumor-vs-normal selectivity)?

variant_level_interpretation.label: Variant level interpretation
variant_level_interpretation.plain_english: For target, which specific variants are oncogenic (vs VUS/benign) and which confer therapy resistance?

structure_druggability.label: Structure druggability
structure_druggability.plain_english: Are target's known hotspots in druggable pockets, and how confident is the structural context?

degradation_feasibility.label: Degradation feasibility
degradation_feasibility.plain_english: Is target a tractable degradation substrate (PROTAC/molecular-glue feasibility)?

model_availability.label: Model availability
model_availability.plain_english: How many patient-derived (HCMI) models exist for the indication to preclinically validate a nomination?

cis_protein_dosage_coupling.label: Cis protein dosage coupling
cis_protein_dosage_coupling.plain_english: Does the target's own copy-number predict its own protein abundance (protein cis-dosage coupling / amplification dosage preserved at the protein level)?

alteration_clinical_association.label: Alteration clinical association
alteration_clinical_association.plain_english: Does target mutation status stratify patient survival in the indication (prognostic association)?

pathway_node_leverage.label: Pathway node leverage
pathway_node_leverage.plain_english: Given the biology, is target the best NODE to hit within its complex / pathway neighbourhood, or is it dominated by a more-dependent / more-tractable member (lineage-scoped, common-essential-excluded)?

surface_density.label: Surface density
surface_density.plain_english: What is estimated surface copies-per-cell, and is it above the TCE-viability threshold?

cross_consortium_dependency.label: Cross consortium dependency
cross_consortium_dependency.plain_english: Do Broad Achilles + Sanger Project Score CRISPR consortia agree the target is a dependency?

reactome_pathway_membership.label: Reactome pathway membership
reactome_pathway_membership.plain_english: Which curated Reactome pathways is target a member of, under which top-level parents?

pmhc_epitope_evidence.label: Pmhc epitope evidence
pmhc_epitope_evidence.plain_english: Does the target have experimentally-validated epitopes in IEDB — peptides observed presented on human HLA and/or recognized by T cells (which class / how many alleles, in a cancer context)?

variant_functional_effect_mave.label: Variant functional effect mave
variant_functional_effect_mave.plain_english: For target, how extensively have its variants been functionally assayed in MAVE experiments, and what is the measured functional-score distribution?

modality_window.label: Modality window
modality_window.plain_english: Is tumor expression high enough relative to the worst essential normal organ to open a therapeutic window at this modality tier?

drug_warning_safety.label: Drug warning safety
drug_warning_safety.plain_english: Have drugs that ENGAGE the target carried FDA black-box warnings or been withdrawn (pharmacovigilance orienting context)?

target_identity.label: Target identity
target_identity.plain_english: Does the symbol resolve to a canonical HGNC/Ensembl/UniProt identity plus curated biology axis?

spatial_surface_protein.label: Spatial surface protein
spatial_surface_protein.plain_english: What is the MEASURED in-situ PROTEIN abundance (GeoMx DSP) of the target in the TUMOUR compartment vs the microenvironment (TME) — is the target protein tumour-enriched or TME-enriched?

tumor_protein_abundance.label: Tumor protein abundance
tumor_protein_abundance.plain_english: Is target present at protein level in tumor vs matched normal (CPTAC MS)?

known_drug_tractability.label: Known drug tractability
known_drug_tractability.plain_english: Has a small-molecule drug been catalogued against target (approved/antineoplastic), and is it in a druggable-genome category?

chemical_combination_synergy.label: Chemical combination synergy

sc_normal_surface_protein.label: Sc normal surface protein

temporal_expression_shift.label: Temporal expression shift

clinvar_germline_pathogenicity_safety.label: Clinvar germline pathogenicity safety

sc_tumor_celltype_expression.label: Sc tumor celltype expression
sc_tumor_celltype_expression.plain_english: In how many cells of each tumor COMPARTMENT (malignant / immune / stromal / endothelial) is target detected at single-cell resolution, and is a detectable tumor signal tumor-cell-intrinsic (malignant)

rnai_lof_dependency.label: Rnai lof dependency

gnomad_lof_constraint.label: Gnomad lof constraint
gnomad_lof_constraint.plain_english: How constrained is target against germline LoF in the gnomAD population (safety)?

spatial_colocalization.label: Spatial colocalization

tumor_vs_normal_percentile_crossing.label: Tumor vs normal percentile crossing
tumor_vs_normal_percentile_crossing.plain_english: What fraction of an indication's tumors express target above the Nth percentile of matched normal (per-sample selectivity)?

cited_literature_evidence.label: Cited literature evidence

cd_antigen_backbone.label: Cd antigen backbone
